2.36.s:
2.176
.. rāma uvāca .. ..
yātrāvidhānamācakṣva sarvadharmabhṛtāṃvara ..
jigīṣūṇāṃ narendrāṇāṃ siddhikāraṇamuttamam .. 1 ..
2.36.d:
2.176
॥ राम उवाच ॥ ॥
यात्राविधानमाचक्ष्व सर्वधर्मभृतांवर ॥
जिगीषूणां नरेन्द्राणां सिद्धिकारणमुत्तमम् ॥ 1 ॥
2.36.m: Rāma said: / Explain the rite of an expedition, O best of all upholders of dharma, / which is the supreme cause of success for kings wishing to conquer.

2.36.s:
puṣkara uvāca ..
saptāhena yadā yātrā bhaviṣyati mahīpateḥ ..
tadā dine tu prathame pūjanīyo vināyakaḥ .. 2 ..
2.36.d:
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
सप्ताहेन यदा यात्रा भविष्यति महीपतेः ॥
तदा दिने तु प्रथमे पूजनीयो विनायकः ॥ 2 ॥
2.36.m: Puṣkara said: / When a king’s expedition is to take place after seven days, / then on the first day Vināyaka should be worshipped

2.36.s:
modakairakṣatairdadhnā kusumaiśca tathā phalaiḥ ..
gandharvāstrairalaṅkārairdhūpairdīpairmanoharaiḥ .. 3 ..
2.36.d:
मोदकैरक्षतैर्दध्ना कुसुमैश्च तथा फलैः ॥
गन्धर्वास्त्रैरलङ्कारैर्धूपैर्दीपैर्मनोहरैः ॥ 3 ॥
2.36.m: with sweetmeats, unhusked rice grains, curd, flowers, and fruits, / with perfumes, garments, ornaments, and delightful incenses and lamps.

2.36.s:
dvitīye'nhi tataḥ kāryaṃ sarvadikpālapūjanam ..
dikpālapūjanaṃ kṛtvā teṣāṃ ca purataḥ sthitaḥ .. 4 ..
2.36.d:
द्वितीयेऽन्हि ततः कार्यं सर्वदिक्पालपूजनम् ॥
दिक्पालपूजनं कृत्वा तेषां च पुरतः स्थितः ॥ 4 ॥
2.36.m: Then on the second day, worship of all the guardians of the directions should be performed. / Having worshipped the guardians of the directions and standing before them,

2.36.s:
śayyāṃ kuśābhiḥ kurvīta sitavastrottaracchadām ..
vikirennāgapuṣpaistāṃ tathā siddhārthakaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 5 ..
2.36.d:
शय्यां कुशाभिः कुर्वीत सितवस्त्रोत्तरच्छदाम् ॥
विकिरेन्नागपुष्पैस्तां तथा सिद्धार्थकैः शुभैः ॥ 5 ॥
2.36.m: he should make a bed with kuśa grass, covered with a white cloth, / and scatter it with nāgapuṣpa flowers and auspicious white mustard seeds.

2.36.s:
tacchīrṣake tu pūjyā śrīrbhadrakālī ca pādayoḥ ..
haraṃ dakṣiṇapārśve tu vāme brahmāṇameva ca .. 6 ..
2.36.d:
तच्छीर्षके तु पूज्या श्रीर्भद्रकाली च पादयोः ॥
हरं दक्षिणपार्श्वे तु वामे ब्रह्माणमेव च ॥ 6 ॥
2.36.m: At its head, Śrī should be worshipped, and Bhadrakālī at the feet; / Hara on the right side, and Brahmā on the left.

2.36.s:
pūjitaṃ kalaśaṃ hṛdyaṃ kuryāduṣṇīṣake dṛḍham ..
nīlapallavasaṃchannaṃ cārupuṣpojjvalaṃ śubham .. 7 ..
2.36.d:
पूजितं कलशं हृद्यं कुर्यादुष्णीषके दृढम् ॥
नीलपल्लवसंछन्नं चारुपुष्पोज्ज्वलं शुभम् ॥ 7 ॥
2.36.m: He should firmly set a charming, consecrated water jar at the head of the bed, / covered with blue shoots, bright with lovely flowers, and auspicious.

2.36.s:
ekakālaṃ haviṣyānnaṃ laghu bhuktvā mahīpatiḥ ..
svayaṃ dakṣiṇapārśve ca mantrametadudīrayet .. 8 ..
2.36.d:
एककालं हविष्यान्नं लघु भुक्त्वा महीपतिः ॥
स्वयं दक्षिणपार्श्वे च मन्त्रमेतदुदीरयेत् ॥ 8 ॥
2.36.m: Having eaten once a light meal of sacrificial food, the king / should lie on his right side and himself recite this mantra:

2.36.s:
namaḥ śambho trinetrāya rudrāya varadāya ca ..
vāmanāya virūpāya svapnādhipataye namaḥ ..9..
2.36.d:
नमः शम्भो त्रिनेत्राय रुद्राय वरदाय च ॥
वामनाय विरूपाय स्वप्नाधिपतये नमः ॥9॥
2.36.m: “Homage to Śambhu, the three-eyed one, to Rudra, the granter of boons, / to the dwarf, to the deformed one, homage to the lord of dreams!

2.36.s:
bhagavandevadeveśa śūlabhṛdvṛṣavāhana ..
iṣṭāniṣṭaṃ samācakṣva svapne suptasya śāśvatam..2.176.10..
2.36.d:
भगवन्देवदेवेश शूलभृद्वृषवाहन ॥
इष्टानिष्टं समाचक्ष्व स्वप्ने सुप्तस्य शाश्वतम्॥2.176.10॥
2.36.m: O blessed Lord, ruler of the gods of gods, trident-bearer whose mount is the bull, / tell me, who am asleep in a dream, truly what is desirable and undesirable!”

2.36.s:
yajjāgrato dūramiti mantramāvartayettataḥ ..
hṛdi nyasya kuśānrājñaḥ prayatastu purohitaḥ ..11..
2.36.d:
यज्जाग्रतो दूरमिति मन्त्रमावर्तयेत्ततः ॥
हृदि न्यस्य कुशान्राज्ञः प्रयतस्तु पुरोहितः ॥11॥
2.36.m: Then the attentive priest, having placed kuśa grass on the king’s chest, / should recite the mantra beginning with “yajjāgrato dūram.”

2.36.s:
tataḥ svapne śubhe dṛṣṭe yātrā deyā tu nānyathā ..
tṛtīye'hani saṃprāpte devaṃ diṅnāthamarcayet..12..
2.36.d:
ततः स्वप्ने शुभे दृष्टे यात्रा देया तु नान्यथा ॥
तृतीयेऽहनि संप्राप्ते देवं दिङ्नाथमर्चयेत्॥12॥
2.36.m: Then, if an auspicious dream is seen, the expedition should be undertaken, but not otherwise. / When the third day arrives, he should worship the lord of the direction—

2.36.s:
ekameva mahābhāga dinanāthaṃ tathā graham ..
yāṃ diśaṃ nṛpatirgacchennāthaṃ tasyāstathaiva tām..13..
2.36.d:
एकमेव महाभाग दिननाथं तथा ग्रहम् ॥
यां दिशं नृपतिर्गच्छेन्नाथं तस्यास्तथैव ताम्॥13॥
2.36.m: just that single one, O fortunate one, the lord of the day, and the planet [governing the direction]; / the king should worship the lord of that direction toward which he intends to go.

2.36.s:
caturthe'hani saṃprāpte grahayāgo vidhīyate..
pañcame'hani saṃprāpte sarvayāgastathaiva ca ..
devatānāṃ svanagare kṛtā yāsāṃ tathālayāḥ ..14..
2.36.d:
चतुर्थेऽहनि संप्राप्ते ग्रहयागो विधीयते॥
पञ्चमेऽहनि संप्राप्ते सर्वयागस्तथैव च ॥
देवतानां स्वनगरे कृता यासां तथालयाः ॥14॥
2.36.m: When the fourth day arrives, a planetary sacrifice is prescribed; / and when the fifth day arrives, a universal sacrifice [is prescribed] / for the deities whose shrines are built in his own city.

2.36.s:
tāsāṃ saṃpūjanaṃ kāryaṃ svapure ye tathā sthitāḥ ..
tatraiva rātrau bhūtānāṃ kartavyaṃ ca tathārcanam .. 15 ..
2.36.d:
तासां संपूजनं कार्यं स्वपुरे ये तथा स्थिताः ॥
तत्रैव रात्रौ भूतानां कर्तव्यं च तथार्चनम् ॥ 15 ॥
2.36.m: Worship should be offered to those deities who dwell in his own city; / and in that very night, worship of the spirits should be performed:

2.36.s:
ekavṛkṣeṣu caityeṣu catvarāṭṭālakeṣu ca ..
catuṣpatheṣu rathyāsu parvatānāṃ guhāsu ca .. 16 ..
2.36.d:
एकवृक्षेषु चैत्येषु चत्वराट्टालकेषु च ॥
चतुष्पथेषु रथ्यासु पर्वतानां गुहासु च ॥ 16 ॥
2.36.m: at solitary trees, caityas, courtyards, watchtowers, / crossroads, streets, mountain caves,

2.36.s:
nadītīreṣu śaileṣu devatāyataneṣu ca ..
teṣāṃ saṃpūjanaṃ kṛtvā svagṛhe tānsamarcayet .. 17 ..
2.36.d:
नदीतीरेषु शैलेषु देवतायतनेषु च ॥
तेषां संपूजनं कृत्वा स्वगृहे तान्समर्चयेत् ॥ 17 ॥
2.36.m: riverbanks, rocky hills, and temples of deities. / Having worshipped them there, he should worship them in his own home.

2.36.s:
tatra kṛtvā tato vācyāḥ pramathā bhūbhujā svayam ..
vāsudevasya devasya tathā saṃkarṣaṇasya ca .. 18 ..
2.36.d:
तत्र कृत्वा ततो वाच्याः प्रमथा भूभुजा स्वयम् ॥
वासुदेवस्य देवस्य तथा संकर्षणस्य च ॥ 18 ॥
2.36.m: Having performed it there, the Pramathas should then be addressed by the king himself: / “The troops of the god Vāsudeva and of Saṃkarṣaṇa,

2.36.s:
pradyumnasyāniruddhasya brahmaṇaḥ śaṅkarasya ca ..
kīnāśaśakravaruṇadhaneśānāṃ tu ye gaṇāḥ .. 19 ..
2.36.d:
प्रद्युम्नस्यानिरुद्धस्य ब्रह्मणः शङ्करस्य च ॥
कीनाशशक्रवरुणधनेशानां तु ये गणाः ॥ 19 ॥
2.36.m: of Pradyumna, of Aniruddha, of Brahmā, and of Śaṅkara; / and those troops of Yama, Indra, Varuṇa, and Kubera;

2.36.s:
vāyośca nirṛtervahnestathā candrārkayośca ye ..
grahāṇāmatha ṛkṣāṇāṃ skandasya ca mahābalāḥ .. 2.176.20 ..
2.36.d:
वायोश्च निरृतेर्वह्नेस्तथा चन्द्रार्कयोश्च ये ॥
ग्रहाणामथ ऋक्षाणां स्कन्दस्य च महाबलाः ॥ 2.176.20 ॥
2.36.m: and those of Vāyu, Nirṛti, Agni, and of the moon and sun; / and those mighty ones of the planets, asterisms, and of Skanda;

2.36.s:
vināyakasya devasya devatānāṃ gaṇāśca ye ..
daityānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ ca sarveṣāmanugāśca ye .. 21 ..
2.36.d:
विनायकस्य देवस्य देवतानां गणाश्च ये ॥
दैत्यानां राक्षसानां च सर्वेषामनुगाश्च ये ॥ 21 ॥
2.36.m: and the troops of the god Vināyaka, and of the gods; / and all those who follow the Daityas and Rākṣasas—

2.36.s:
mahābalā mahākāyā mahāsattvā mahābratāḥ..
aṇimā mahimā prāptiḥ prākāmyena ca saṃyutāḥ..22..
2.36.d:
महाबला महाकाया महासत्त्वा महाब्रताः॥
अणिमा महिमा प्राप्तिः प्राकाम्येन च संयुताः॥22॥
2.36.m: mighty, huge-bodied, of great strength, of great vows, / endowed with lightness, greatness, reach, and freedom of will,

2.36.s:
īśitvena vaśitvena prāptināmnā tathodaye ..
yatra kāmāvasāyitvāttathā yeṣāṃ ca vidyate .. 23 ..
2.36.d:
ईशित्वेन वशित्वेन प्राप्तिनाम्ना तथोदये ॥
यत्र कामावसायित्वात्तथा येषां च विद्यते ॥ 23 ॥
2.36.m: with lordship, mastery, and the power of attainment, / and those in whom the power to suppress desire anywhere exists—

2.36.s:
evamaṣṭaguṇaiśvaryasaṃyutā bhīmavikramāḥ ..
nānāsattvaśirogrīvā nānāpraharaṇāyudhāḥ .. 24 ..
2.36.d:
एवमष्टगुणैश्वर्यसंयुता भीमविक्रमाः ॥
नानासत्त्वशिरोग्रीवा नानाप्रहरणायुधाः ॥ 24 ॥
2.36.m: thus endowed with the eightfold superhuman powers, of terrifying valor, / having heads and necks of various creatures, bearing various weapons and arms,

2.36.s:
nānāvirāgavasanā nānāsattvavapurdharāḥ ..
tathā nānāvidhāhārā mahāceṣṭā mahābalāḥ .. 25 ..
2.36.d:
नानाविरागवसना नानासत्त्ववपुर्धराः ॥
तथा नानाविधाहारा महाचेष्टा महाबलाः ॥ 25 ॥
2.36.m: dressed in garments of various colors, wearing the forms of various creatures, / eating various kinds of food, of great deeds and mighty strength,

2.36.s:
bhaktānukampino vīrā varadāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ ..
pramathāḥ parigṛhṇantu upakāraṃ namo'stu vaḥ ..
saputrāmātyabhṛtyo'haṃ sadāraḥ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ .. 26 ..
2.36.d:
भक्तानुकम्पिनो वीरा वरदाः कामरूपिणः ॥
प्रमथाः परिगृह्णन्तु उपकारं नमोऽस्तु वः ॥
सपुत्रामात्यभृत्योऽहं सदारः शरणं गतः ॥ 26 ॥
2.36.m: compassionate to devotees, heroic, granters of boons, able to assume any form at will— / may the Pramathas accept this offering; homage be to you! / Together with my sons, ministers, servants, and wife, I have taken refuge.

2.36.s:
rakṣantu māṃ mahābhāgā gṛhe yuddhe tathādhvani ..
camūnāṃ pṛṣṭhato gatvā nāśayadhvaṃ tathā ripūn .. 27 ..
2.36.d:
रक्षन्तु मां महाभागा गृहे युद्धे तथाध्वनि ॥
चमूनां पृष्ठतो गत्वा नाशयध्वं तथा रिपून् ॥ 27 ॥
2.36.m: May the fortunate ones protect me at home, in battle, and on the road! / Going behind my armies, destroy my enemies!

2.36.s:
svapne śubhāśubhaṃ vāpi kathayadhvaṃ samāhitāḥ ..
vinivṛttaśca dāsyāmi dattādabhyadhikaṃ balim .. 28 ..
2.36.d:
स्वप्ने शुभाशुभं वापि कथयध्वं समाहिताः ॥
विनिवृत्तश्च दास्यामि दत्तादभ्यधिकं बलिम् ॥ 28 ॥
2.36.m: Concentrated in mind, tell me in a dream what is auspicious or inauspicious. / And when I have returned, I will offer a sacrifice greater than what was given!”

2.36.s:
vinivṛttena dātavyaḥ sa ca yatnena bhūbhujā ..
pūrvavacca tathā rātrau svapnaprārthanamiṣyate .. .. 29 ..
2.36.d:
विनिवृत्तेन दातव्यः स च यत्नेन भूभुजा ॥
पूर्ववच्च तथा रात्रौ स्वप्नप्रार्थनमिष्यते ॥ ॥ 29 ॥
2.36.m: And that [offering] must diligently be given by the king upon his return; / and in the night, as before, prayer for a dream is prescribed.

2.36.s:
ṣaṣṭhe'hani jayasnānaṃ kartavyaṃ ca tathā bhavet ..
vidhirasyābhiṣekārthaḥ sarva eva vidhīyate .. 2.176.30 ..
2.36.d:
षष्ठेऽहनि जयस्नानं कर्तव्यं च तथा भवेत् ॥
विधिरस्याभिषेकार्थः सर्व एव विधीयते ॥ 2.176.30 ॥
2.36.m: On the sixth day, the victory-bath should be performed; / the entire procedure prescribed for royal consecration is enjoined for this.

2.36.s:
tato yātrādine prāpte kṣaurakarma vivarjayet ..
mudraṇaṃ bhedanaṃ caiva tathā ca nakhakṛntanam .. 31 ..
2.36.d:
ततो यात्रादिने प्राप्ते क्षौरकर्म विवर्जयेत् ॥
मुद्रणं भेदनं चैव तथा च नखकृन्तनम् ॥ 31 ॥
2.36.m: Then, when the day of the expedition arrives, he should avoid shaving, / sealing, perforating, and also clipping nails,

2.36.s:
abhyaṅgaṃ gṛhakāryaṃ ca krodhaśokau ca kaṅkatam ..
yātavyaṃ yena tenātha taduktaṃ snānamācaret .. 32 ..
2.36.d:
अभ्यङ्गं गृहकार्यं च क्रोधशोकौ च कङ्कतम् ॥
यातव्यं येन तेनाथ तदुक्तं स्नानमाचरेत् ॥ 32 ॥
2.36.m: anointing the body with oil, household chores, anger, sorrow, and combing the hair; / whichever bath is prescribed for the direction to be traversed, he should perform that.

2.36.s:
snātaḥ śuklāmbaraḥ sragvī tathā śvetānulepanaḥ ..
citrābharaṇavānrājā dūrvāpallavalācchanaḥ .. 33 ..
2.36.d:
स्नातः शुक्लाम्बरः स्रग्वी तथा श्वेतानुलेपनः ॥
चित्राभरणवान्राजा दूर्वापल्लवलाच्छनः ॥ 33 ॥
2.36.m: Bathed, wearing white garments, garlanded, anointed with white unguents, / wearing various ornaments, adorned with dūrvā grass shoots,

2.36.s:
pūjayitvā mahābhāgaṃ devadevaṃ trivikramam ..
juhuyācca tathā vahnau susamiddhe purohitaḥ .. 34 ..
2.36.d:
पूजयित्वा महाभागं देवदेवं त्रिविक्रमम् ॥
जुहुयाच्च तथा वह्नौ सुसमिद्धे पुरोहितः ॥ 34 ॥
2.36.m: having worshipped Trivikrama, the fortunate god of gods, / the priest should make offerings in the well-kindled fire:

2.36.s:
āyuṣyamabhayaṃ caiva tathā svastyayanaṃ gaṇam ..
śarmavarmagaṇaṃ caiva tathā pratirathaṃ śubhama .. 35 ..
2.36.d:
आयुष्यमभयं चैव तथा स्वस्त्ययनं गणम् ॥
शर्मवर्मगणं चैव तथा प्रतिरथं शुभम ॥ 35 ॥
2.36.m: with the Āyuṣya, Abhaya, and Svastyayana hymn-groups, / with the Śarmavarman hymn-group, and the auspicious Pratiratha hymn,

2.36.s:
śakunaṃ ca tathā sūktaṃ sūktaṃ vaiṣṇavameva ca ..
tathāgnilakṣaṇotpattau śubhe yāyānmahīpatiḥ .. 36 ..
2.36.d:
शकुनं च तथा सूक्तं सूक्तं वैष्णवमेव च ॥
तथाग्निलक्षणोत्पत्तौ शुभे यायान्महीपतिः ॥ 36 ॥
2.36.m: and the Śakuna hymn, and the Vaiṣṇava hymn; / and when auspicious omens appear in the fire, the king should set out.

2.36.s:
nakṣatrasya diśaścaiva naivedyaṃ yatprakīrtitam ..
tadeva nṛpatiḥ prāśya yātrāṃ vidyādyathāvidhi .. 37 ..
2.36.d:
नक्षत्रस्य दिशश्चैव नैवेद्यं यत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
तदेव नृपतिः प्राश्य यात्रां विद्याद्यथाविधि ॥ 37 ॥
2.36.m: Having eaten the food offering prescribed / for the lunar asterism and the direction, the king should undertake the expedition according to the ritual.

2.36.s:
ahṛdyaṃ makṣikākeśakīṭayuktaṃ vivarjayet ..
dagdhe ca varjayedyātrāṃ deyā bhavati cānyathā .. 38 ..
2.36.d:
अहृद्यं मक्षिकाकेशकीटयुक्तं विवर्जयेत् ॥
दग्धे च वर्जयेद्यात्रां देया भवति चान्यथा ॥ 38 ॥
2.36.m: He should avoid food that is disagreeable, contaminated with flies, hair, or worms; / and if it is burnt, he should abandon the expedition, which may be undertaken otherwise.

2.36.s:
tatastu rājaliṅgānāṃ cāyudhānāṃ tathaiva ca ..
nīrājanoktamantraistu sarvāṃstānabhimantrayet .. 39 ..
2.36.d:
ततस्तु राजलिङ्गानां चायुधानां तथैव च ॥
नीराजनोक्तमन्त्रैस्तु सर्वांस्तानभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥ 39 ॥
2.36.m: Then, with the mantras prescribed for the waving of lights, / he should consecrate all the royal insignia and weapons.

2.36.s:
daivavitprayato bhūtvā rājā vātha purohitaḥ ..
teṣāṃ saṃpūjanaṃ kṛtvā daivajñaṃ sapurohitam .. 2.176.40 ..
2.36.d:
दैववित्प्रयतो भूत्वा राजा वाथ पुरोहितः ॥
तेषां संपूजनं कृत्वा दैवज्ञं सपुरोहितम् ॥ 2.176.40 ॥
2.36.m: The astrologer having become concentrated in mind, or the king, or the royal chaplain, / having worshipped them, the king should worship the astrologer together with the chaplain,

2.36.s:
dhanena pūjayedrājā dakṣiṇābhirdvijottamān ..
tataḥ puṇyāhaghoṣeṇa dvijānāṃ hatakalmaṣaḥ .. 41 ..
2.36.d:
धनेन पूजयेद्राजा दक्षिणाभिर्द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
ततः पुण्याहघोषेण द्विजानां हतकल्मषः ॥ 41 ॥
2.36.m: and the foremost of the twice-born with wealth and sacrificial fees. / Then, his sins destroyed by the twice-born's proclamation of an auspicious day,

2.36.s:
maṅgalālambhanaṃ kṛtvā mantrametaṃ niśāmayan ..
ādityā vasavo rudrā viśvedevā marudgaṇāḥ .. 42 ..
2.36.d:
मङ्गलालम्भनं कृत्वा मन्त्रमेतं निशामयन् ॥
आदित्या वसवो रुद्रा विश्वेदेवा मरुद्गणाः ॥ 42 ॥
2.36.m: having touched auspicious items while listening to this mantra: / 'May the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvedevas, and host of Maruts,

2.36.s:
lokapālāḥ sagandharvā nadyaḥ śailā mahī dvijāḥ ..
agniḥ svāhā svadhā homaḥ skando brahmā prajāpatiḥ .. 43 ..
2.36.d:
लोकपालाः सगन्धर्वा नद्यः शैला मही द्विजाः ॥
अग्निः स्वाहा स्वधा होमः स्कन्दो ब्रह्मा प्रजापतिः ॥ 43 ॥
2.36.m: the guardians of the worlds together with the gandharvas, rivers, mountains, the earth, the twice-born, / Agni, Svāhā, Svadhā, the burnt offering, Skanda, Brahmā, Prajāpati,

2.36.s:
muhūrtāstithayo bhāni vedāḥ sāyanavatsarāḥ ..
gāvaḥ sarasvatī devī dīrghamāyurdiśantu te ..44 ..
2.36.d:
मुहूर्तास्तिथयो भानि वेदाः सायनवत्सराः ॥
गावः सरस्वती देवी दीर्घमायुर्दिशन्तु ते ॥44 ॥
2.36.m: the muhūrtas, lunar days, lunar mansions, Vedas, solar years, / cows, and goddess Sarasvatī bestow long life upon you!

2.36.s:
jagatsṛjo'tha yā siddhirbabhūva brahmaṇaḥ purā ..
jagajjiṣṇośca yā viṣṇoḥ siddhiryāsīttrivikrame .. 45 ..
2.36.d:
जगत्सृजोऽथ या सिद्धिर्बभूव ब्रह्मणः पुरा ॥
जगज्जिष्णोश्च या विष्णोः सिद्धिर्यासीत्त्रिविक्रमे ॥ 45 ॥
2.36.m: The success that was attained of old by Brahmā the creator of the universe, / and the success of Viṣṇu the conqueror of the universe in his three strides,

2.36.s:
asuraiśvaryanāśe ca babhūva tryambakasya yā ..
siddhistridarśavṛddhyarthaṃ tripurāntakṛtaḥ purā .. 46 ..
2.36.d:
असुरैश्वर्यनाशे च बभूव त्र्यम्बकस्य या ॥
सिद्धिस्त्रिदर्शवृद्ध्यर्थं त्रिपुरान्तकृतः पुरा ॥ 46 ॥
2.36.m: and that which was attained of old by Tryambaka, the destroyer of Tripura, / in destroying the dominion of the asuras for the increase of the gods,

2.36.s:
śakre vṛtravadhe yāvatskande devārisaṃkṣaye ..
tāṃ prāpnuhi sadā siddhiṃ sā ca yātrāstu te sadā .. 47 ..
2.36.d:
शक्रे वृत्रवधे यावत्स्कन्दे देवारिसंक्षये ॥
तां प्राप्नुहि सदा सिद्धिं सा च यात्रास्तु ते सदा ॥ 47 ॥
2.36.m: and as much [success as was] in Śakra in the slaying of Vṛtra, and in Skanda in the destruction of the enemies of the gods— / may you attain that eternal success, and may that expedition always be [successful] for you!

2.36.s:
rakṣantu sarvataḥ sarve devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ ..
iti coktvā śubhāṃ vācaṃ gṛhītvā saśaraṃ dhanuḥ .. .. 48 ..
2.36.d:
रक्षन्तु सर्वतः सर्वे देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः ॥
इति चोक्त्वा शुभां वाचं गृहीत्वा सशरं धनुः ॥ ॥ 48 ॥
2.36.m: May all the gods, led by Śakra, protect [you] on all sides!' / Having spoken this auspicious utterance and having taken a bow with arrows,

2.36.s:
dhanvanāgetimantreṇa daivajñasya karātsvayam ..
tadviṣṇoḥ paramityeva śṛṇvanmantramanuttamam .. 49 ..
2.36.d:
धन्वनागेतिमन्त्रेण दैवज्ञस्य करात्स्वयम् ॥
तद्विष्णोः परमित्येव शृण्वन्मन्त्रमनुत्तमम् ॥ 49 ॥
2.36.m: with the mantra 'By the bow...', directly from the hand of the astrologer, / listening to the unsurpassed mantra, 'That supreme [step] of Viṣṇu...',

2.36.s:
paiṣṭe ripumukhe dadyātprathamaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ padam ..
padadvātriṃśakaṃ gatvā viṣṇuprācyādiṣu tvatha .. 2.176.50 ..
2.36.d:
पैष्टे रिपुमुखे दद्यात्प्रथमं दक्षिणं पदम् ॥
पदद्वात्रिंशकं गत्वा विष्णुप्राच्यादिषु त्वथ ॥ 2.176.50 ॥
2.36.m: he should place his right foot first on the dough-made face of the enemy. / Then, having advanced thirty-two steps toward Viṣṇu, the east, and the other [directions],

2.36.s:
nāgaṃ rathaṃ hayaṃ caiva yuñjāne cāruhetkramāta ..
āruhya sumanā gacchedvādyaghoṣeṇa bhūriṇā .. 51 ..
2.36.d:
नागं रथं हयं चैव युञ्जाने चारुहेत्क्रमात ॥
आरुह्य सुमना गच्छेद्वाद्यघोषेण भूरिणा ॥ 51 ॥
2.36.m: he should mount in turn an elephant, a chariot, and a horse while they are yoked. / Having mounted, he should set forth glad of mind, with a loud clamour of musical instruments.

2.36.s:
sa niṣkramya mahānīśo na pṛṣṭhamavalokayet ..
maṅgalāni tataḥ paśyanspṛñchṛṇvañśanairvrajet .. 52 ..
2.36.d:
स निष्क्रम्य महानीशो न पृष्ठमवलोकयेत् ॥
मङ्गलानि ततः पश्यन्स्पृञ्छृण्वञ्शनैर्व्रजेत् ॥ 52 ॥
2.36.m: Having set out, the great lord must not look behind. / Looking upon, touching, and hearing auspicious things, he should then proceed slowly.

2.36.s:
krośamātraṃ tato gacchennādhikaṃ tu kadācana ..
gatvā deśe śubhe tiṣṭhetpūjayitvā suradvijān .. 53 ..
2.36.d:
क्रोशमात्रं ततो गच्छेन्नाधिकं तु कदाचन ॥
गत्वा देशे शुभे तिष्ठेत्पूजयित्वा सुरद्विजान् ॥ 53 ॥
2.36.m: He should then go only a krośa, never further. / Having arrived, he should stay in an auspicious place after worshipping the gods and twice-born.

2.36.s:
tataḥ krameṇa gacchecca paradeśaṃ mahīpatiḥ ..
ātmasainyānurūpeṇa kṛtarakṣaḥ pathā dvija .. 54 ..
2.36.d:
ततः क्रमेण गच्छेच्च परदेशं महीपतिः ॥
आत्मसैन्यानुरूपेण कृतरक्षः पथा द्विज ॥ 54 ॥
2.36.m: Then, O twice-born, the ruler of the earth should proceed by degrees to foreign territory / along a route secured in keeping with his own army.

2.36.s:
trirātramuṣito gacchedbhūyo nakṣatrasampadā ..
yavasaindhavatoyānāṃ rakṣako viṣadūṣaṇāt .. 55 ..
2.36.d:
त्रिरात्रमुषितो गच्छेद्भूयो नक्षत्रसम्पदा ॥
यवसैन्धवतोयानां रक्षको विषदूषणात् ॥ 55 ॥
2.36.m: Having stayed three nights, he should proceed further under a favourable constellation, / guarding barley, salt, and water from contamination by poison.

2.36.s:
parānabhimukho gacchetprabhūtayavasaindhavaḥ ..
svairacaṃkramaṇaṃ śayyāṃ bhāṇḍaprakṣepaṇaṃ tathā .. 56 ..
2.36.d:
परानभिमुखो गच्छेत्प्रभूतयवसैन्धवः ॥
स्वैरचंक्रमणं शय्यां भाण्डप्रक्षेपणं तथा ॥ 56 ॥
2.36.m: He should advance facing the enemies, having abundant barley and salt. / He should make his free walking, sleeping, the storing of baggage,

2.36.s:
bhojana taṃ sukhaṃ kuryātpratilomaṃ na cācareta ..
rājāpyamitradeśe tu deśācāraṃ na laṃghayet .. 57 ..
2.36.d:
भोजन तं सुखं कुर्यात्प्रतिलोमं न चाचरेत ॥
राजाप्यमित्रदेशे तु देशाचारं न लंघयेत् ॥ 57 ॥
2.36.m: and dining comfortable, and should not act contrary to what is right. / Even in enemy territory, the king should not transgress the local customs.

2.36.s:
devatāpūjanaṃ kuyārnnocchiṃdyāddāvamatra tu ..
kulastriyaṃ ca tanvīṃ ca vṛddhāṃ naivāpamānayeta .. 58 ..
2.36.d:
देवतापूजनं कुयार्न्नोच्छिंद्याद्दावमत्र तु ॥
कुलस्त्रियं च तन्वीं च वृद्धां नैवापमानयेत ॥ 58 ॥
2.36.m: He should perform the worship of the deities, and must not destroy forests there. / He must never disrespect a noble woman, a young girl, or an old woman.

2.36.s:
kulīnamabhinindettu na vai nṛpativaṃśajam ..
na karṇanāsācchedāṃśca na tathā netrabhedanam ..
kālavinmantribhiṣajorvākyaṃ kuryānmahīpatiḥ .. 59 ..
2.36.d:
कुलीनमभिनिन्देत्तु न वै नृपतिवंशजम् ॥
न कर्णनासाच्छेदांश्च न तथा नेत्रभेदनम् ॥
कालविन्मन्त्रिभिषजोर्वाक्यं कुर्यान्महीपतिः ॥ 59 ॥
2.36.m: He should not revile a well-born man, nor indeed one born of a royal line. / There must be no severing of ears and nose, nor blinding of eyes. / The ruler of the earth should heed the words of his astrologer, counselors, and physician.

2.36.s:
tataḥ kramātprāpya purīṃ svakīyāṃ baliṃ tu dadyādadhikāṃ puroktām ..
kuryānmahīṃ yūpasurālayāṃkāṃ svarlokamicchanpṛthivīṃ samagrām .. 2.176.60 ..
2.177
rāma uvāca ..
sāṃgrāmikamahaṃ tvattaḥ śrotumicchāmi bhūbhujaḥ ..
sarvaṃ vetsi mahābhāga tvaṃ deva parameṣṭhivat .. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
dvitīye'hani saṃgrāmo bhaviṣyati yadā tadā ..
gajāśvānsnāpayedrājā sarvauṣadhijalaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 2 ..
gandhamālyairalaṃkuryātpūjayecca yathāvidhi ..
nṛsiṃhaṃ pūjayedviṣṇuṃ rājaliṅgānyaśeṣataḥ .. 3 ..
chatraṃ dhvajaṃ patākāśca dharmāścaiva mahābhuja ..
āyudhāni ca sarvāṇi tathā pūjyāni bhūbhujā .. 4 ..
teṣāṃ sampūjanaṃ kṛtvā rātrau pramathapūjanam ..
kṛtvā tu prārthayedrājā vijayāyetaro yathā .. 5 ..5..
pramathāṃśca sahāyārthe dharaṇīṃ ca mahābhuja ..
bhiṣakpurohitāmātyamantrimadhye tathā svapet .. 6 ..
2.36.d:
ततः क्रमात्प्राप्य पुरीं स्वकीयां बलिं तु दद्यादधिकां पुरोक्ताम् ॥
कुर्यान्महीं यूपसुरालयांकां स्वर्लोकमिच्छन्पृथिवीं समग्राम् ॥ 2.176.60 ॥
2.177
राम उवाच ॥
सांग्रामिकमहं त्वत्तः श्रोतुमिच्छामि भूभुजः ॥
सर्वं वेत्सि महाभाग त्वं देव परमेष्ठिवत् ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
द्वितीयेऽहनि संग्रामो भविष्यति यदा तदा ॥
गजाश्वान्स्नापयेद्राजा सर्वौषधिजलैः शुभैः ॥ 2 ॥
गन्धमाल्यैरलंकुर्यात्पूजयेच्च यथाविधि ॥
नृसिंहं पूजयेद्विष्णुं राजलिङ्गान्यशेषतः ॥ 3 ॥
छत्रं ध्वजं पताकाश्च धर्माश्चैव महाभुज ॥
आयुधानि च सर्वाणि तथा पूज्यानि भूभुजा ॥ 4 ॥
तेषां सम्पूजनं कृत्वा रात्रौ प्रमथपूजनम् ॥
कृत्वा तु प्रार्थयेद्राजा विजयायेतरो यथा ॥ 5 ॥5॥
प्रमथांश्च सहायार्थे धरणीं च महाभुज ॥
भिषक्पुरोहितामात्यमन्त्रिमध्ये तथा स्वपेत् ॥ 6 ॥
2.36.m:
Then, having reached his own city in due course, he should make an offering greater than previously mentioned; / desiring the celestial world and the whole earth, he should mark the earth with sacrificial posts and temples of the gods.
Rāma said: / I wish to hear from you about what pertains to battle for an earth-ruler. / O fortunate one, divine being, you know everything like Parameṣṭhin.
Puṣkara said: / When battle is to take place on the second day, / then the king should bathe his elephants and horses with auspicious waters containing all herbs.
He should adorn them with scents and garlands and worship them according to the rule. / He should worship Nṛsiṃha Viṣṇu, and all the royal insignia without exception:
the umbrella, the standard, the banners, and the righteous laws, O mighty-armed one. / And all weapons likewise should be worshipped by the ruler of the earth.
Having performed their worship, having then worshipped the Pramathas at night, / the king should pray for victory as one other [would],
and [pray to] the Pramathas and the earth for assistance, O mighty-armed one. / He should then sleep amidst the physician, chaplain, ministers, and counselors,

2.36.s:
saṃyato brahmacārī ca nṛsiṃhaṃ saṃsmaranharim..
rātrau dṛṣṭe śubhe svapne samarārambhamācaret .. 7 ..
rātriśeṣe samutthāya snātaḥ sarvauṣadhī jalaiḥ ..
pūjayitvā nṛsiṃhaṃ tu vāhanāḍhyamaśeṣataḥ .. 8 ..
purodhasā hutaṃ paśyejjvalitaṃ jātavedasam ..
purodhāḥ pūrvavattatra mantrāṃstu juhuyāttataḥ ..9 ..
dakṣiṇābhiḥ śucirviprānpūjayetpṛthivīpatiḥ ..
tatonulimpedgātrāṇi gandhadvāreti pārthivaḥ .. 2.177.10..
candanāgurukarpūrakāntākālīyakaiḥ śubhaiḥ ..
mūrtiṃ kaṇṭhe samālabhya rocanāṃ ca tathā śubhām..11..
āyuṣyaṃ varcasaṃ caiva mantreṇānena mantritamam..
alaṅkaraṇamābaddhyācchriyaṃ dhāturiti srajam .. 12..
yā oṣadhaya ityevaṃ dhārayedoṣadhīḥ śubhāḥ ..
navo naveti vastraṃ ca kārpāsaṃ bibhṛyācchubham ..13..
2.36.d:
संयतो ब्रह्मचारी च नृसिंहं संस्मरन्हरिम्॥
रात्रौ दृष्टे शुभे स्वप्ने समरारम्भमाचरेत् ॥ 7 ॥
रात्रिशेषे समुत्थाय स्नातः सर्वौषधी जलैः ॥
पूजयित्वा नृसिंहं तु वाहनाढ्यमशेषतः ॥ 8 ॥
पुरोधसा हुतं पश्येज्ज्वलितं जातवेदसम् ॥
पुरोधाः पूर्ववत्तत्र मन्त्रांस्तु जुहुयात्ततः ॥9 ॥
दक्षिणाभिः शुचिर्विप्रान्पूजयेत्पृथिवीपतिः ॥
ततोनुलिम्पेद्गात्राणि गन्धद्वारेति पार्थिवः ॥ 2.177.10॥
चन्दनागुरुकर्पूरकान्ताकालीयकैः शुभैः ॥
मूर्तिं कण्ठे समालभ्य रोचनां च तथा शुभाम्॥11॥
आयुष्यं वर्चसं चैव मन्त्रेणानेन मन्त्रितमम्॥
अलङ्करणमाबद्ध्याच्छ्रियं धातुरिति स्रजम् ॥ 12॥
या ओषधय इत्येवं धारयेदोषधीः शुभाः ॥
नवो नवेति वस्त्रं च कार्पासं बिभृयाच्छुभम् ॥13॥
2.36.m:
restrained, celibate, and meditating on Nṛsiṃha Hari. / When an auspicious dream has been seen at night, he should initiate the battle.
Rising at the end of the night, bathed with waters containing all herbs, / and having worshipped Nṛsiṃha and all the mounts in full,
he should behold the blazed fire offered into by the chaplain. / The chaplain should then offer mantras there as before.
Pure, the lord of the earth should worship the brahmins with sacrificial fees. / Then the king should anoint his limbs with the 'Fragrant gate...' [mantra],
with auspicious sandal, agallochum, camphor, and kāntā-kālīyaka. / Having applied auspicious yellow orpiment onto his image and throat,
he should put on ornaments that give long life and radiance, consecrated with this mantra, / and a garland with 'The glory of the creator...';
he should put on auspicious herbs with 'Which herbs...', / and should put on an auspicious cotton garment with 'New and new...';

2.36.s:
aindrāgneti tato carma dhanvanāgeti vai dhanuḥ..
tato rājñaḥ samādadyātsaśarantvabhimantritam..14..
kuñjaraṃ vā rathaṃ cāśvamāruhedabhimantritam..
āruhya śibirādrājā niṣkramya samaye śubhe..15..
deśe tvadṛśyaḥ śatrūṇāṃ kuryātprakṛtikalpanām ..
saṃhatānyodhayedalpā kāmaṃ vistārayedbahūn ..16..
sūcīmukhamanīkaṃ syādalpānāṃ bahubhiḥ saha ..
vyūhāḥ prāṇyaṅgarūpāśca dravyarūpāśca kalpitāḥ..17..
gāruḍo makaravyūhaścakraṃ śyenastathaiva ca..
ardhacandraśca candraśca śakaṭavyūha eva ca..18..
vyūhaśca sarvatobhadraḥ sūcīvyūhastathaiva ca ..
padmaśca maṇḍalavyūhaḥ prādhānyena prakīrtitāḥ..19..
vyūhānāmatha sarveṣāṃ pañcadhā sainyakalpanā ..

2.36.d:
ऐन्द्राग्नेति ततो चर्म धन्वनागेति वै धनुः॥
ततो राज्ञः समादद्यात्सशरन्त्वभिमन्त्रितम्॥14॥
कुञ्जरं वा रथं चाश्वमारुहेदभिमन्त्रितम्॥
आरुह्य शिबिराद्राजा निष्क्रम्य समये शुभे॥15॥
देशे त्वदृश्यः शत्रूणां कुर्यात्प्रकृतिकल्पनाम् ॥
संहतान्योधयेदल्पा कामं विस्तारयेद्बहून् ॥16॥
सूचीमुखमनीकं स्यादल्पानां बहुभिः सह ॥
व्यूहाः प्राण्यङ्गरूपाश्च द्रव्यरूपाश्च कल्पिताः॥17॥
गारुडो मकरव्यूहश्चक्रं श्येनस्तथैव च॥
अर्धचन्द्रश्च चन्द्रश्च शकटव्यूह एव च॥18॥
व्यूहश्च सर्वतोभद्रः सूचीव्यूहस्तथैव च ॥
पद्मश्च मण्डलव्यूहः प्राधान्येन प्रकीर्तिताः॥19॥
व्यूहानामथ सर्वेषां पञ्चधा सैन्यकल्पना ॥
द्वौ पक्षौ बन्धपक्षौ द्वावौरस्यः पञ्चमो भवेत्॥2.177.20॥
2.36.m:
then [he should put on] armour with 'O Indra and Agni...', and indeed take up a bow with 'By the bow...'. / Then he should take for the king [the bow] with arrows consecrated with mantras.
He should mount an elephant, a chariot, or a horse consecrated with mantras. / Having mounted, the king, coming forth from the camp at an auspicious time,
invisible to the enemies in that region, should arrange his force. / He should make the few fight tightly packed, and may spread out the many at will.
The needle-faced array should be [used] for the few against the many. / Battle-arrays are formed in the shapes of living beings' limbs and in the forms of objects:
the eagle-array, crocodile-array, wheel, and likewise the falcon, / the half-moon, the full moon, and the cart-array,
and the array auspicious on all sides, and likewise the needle-array, / the lotus and the circle-array are proclaimed as the principal ones.
Now, the deployment of troops in all battle-arrays is fivefold: / two wings, two flanks, and the chest would be the fifth.

2.36.s:
anena yadi vā dvābhyāṃ bhāgābhyāṃ yuddhamācaret..
bhāgatrayaṃ sthāpayettu teṣāṃ rakṣārthameva ca..21..
na vyūhe kalpanā kāryā rājño bhavati karhicit ..
patracchede phalacchede vṛkṣacchedāvakalpane..22..
punaḥ prarohamāyāti mūlacchede vinaśyati ..
svayaṃ rājñā na yoddhavyamapi sarvāstraśālinā..23..
nityaṃ loke hi dṛśyante śaktebhyaḥ śaktimāttarāḥ ..
sainyasya paścāttiṣṭhettu krośamātre mahīpatiḥ..24..
bhagnasandhāraṇaṃ tatra yodhānāṃ parikīrtitam ..
pradhānabhaṅge sainyasya nāvasthānaṃ vidhīyate .. 25 ..
na bhagnānpīḍayecchatrūnekāyanagatā hi te ..
maraṇe niścitāḥ sarve hanyuḥ śatrūṃścamūrapi .. 26 ..
śaṭābhaṅgacchalenāpi nayati svabhuvaṃ parām ..
teṣāṃ svabhūmisaṃsthānāṃ vadhaḥ syātsukarastadā .. 27 ..
2.36.d:
अनेन यदि वा द्वाभ्यां भागाभ्यां युद्धमाचरेत्॥
भागत्रयं स्थापयेत्तु तेषां रक्षार्थमेव च॥21॥
न व्यूहे कल्पना कार्या राज्ञो भवति कर्हिचित् ॥
पत्रच्छेदे फलच्छेदे वृक्षच्छेदावकल्पने॥22॥
पुनः प्ररोहमायाति मूलच्छेदे विनश्यति ॥
स्वयं राज्ञा न योद्धव्यमपि सर्वास्त्रशालिना॥23॥
नित्यं लोके हि दृश्यन्ते शक्तेभ्यः शक्तिमात्तराः ॥
सैन्यस्य पश्चात्तिष्ठेत्तु क्रोशमात्रे महीपतिः॥24॥
भग्नसन्धारणं तत्र योधानां परिकीर्तितम् ॥
प्रधानभङ्गे सैन्यस्य नावस्थानं विधीयते ॥ 25 ॥
न भग्नान्पीडयेच्छत्रूनेकायनगता हि ते ॥
मरणे निश्चिताः सर्वे हन्युः शत्रूंश्चमूरपि ॥ 26 ॥
शटाभङ्गच्छलेनापि नयति स्वभुवं पराम् ॥
तेषां स्वभूमिसंस्थानां वधः स्यात्सुकरस्तदा ॥ 27 ॥
2.36.m:
One should fight with this [division] or with two divisions; / but one should station three divisions solely for their protection.
The king should never be placed in the battle array. / When leaves are cut, when fruit is cut, when the branches of a tree are pruned,
it shoots forth again, but when the root is cut, it perishes. / The king should not fight personally, even if possessed of all weapons.
For in the world there are always seen those who are mightier than the mighty. / The ruler of the earth should remain behind the army, just a krośa away.
Rallying broken warriors there is declared [his duty]. / If the leader is broken, no rallying of the army is prescribed.
He should not harass broken enemies, for they have recourse to desperate measures; / resolved on death, they might all kill the enemies and the army as well.
Even by the pretence of a rogue retreat, [a commander] leads [the enemy] to his own advantageous ground. / Then, when they are stationed on his own ground, their slaughter will be easy.

2.36.s:
na saṃhatārtaviralānyodhānvyūhe prakalpayet ..
āyudhānāṃ tu saṃmardo yathā na syātparasparam .. 28 ..
tathā tu kalpanā kāryā yodhānāṃ bhṛgunandana ..
bhettukāmaḥ parānīkaṃ saṃhataireva bhedayet..29..
bhedarakṣāpareṇāpi kartavyā saṃhatā tathā ..
svecchayā kalpayedvyūhaṃ jñātvā vā ripukalpitam..2.177.30..
vyūhe bhedāvahaṃ kuryādripuvyūhasya pārthivaḥ ..
gajasya deyā rakṣārthaṃ catvārastu rathā dvija..31..
rathasya cāśvāścatvāro'śvasya tasya ca varmiṇaḥ ..
varmibhiśca samāstatra dhanvinaḥ parikīrtitāḥ..32..
purastāccarmiṇo deyā deyāstadanu dhanvinaḥ ..
dhanvināmanu cāśvīyaṃ rathāṃstadanu yojayet ..33..
rathānāṃ kuñjarāścānu dātavyāḥ pṛthivīkṣitā ..
padātikuñjarāśvānāṃ varma kāryaṃ prayatnataḥ ..34..
2.36.d:
न संहतार्तविरलान्योधान्व्यूहे प्रकल्पयेत् ॥
आयुधानां तु संमर्दो यथा न स्यात्परस्परम् ॥ 28 ॥
तथा तु कल्पना कार्या योधानां भृगुनन्दन ॥
भेत्तुकामः परानीकं संहतैरेव भेदयेत्॥29॥
भेदरक्षापरेणापि कर्तव्या संहता तथा ॥
स्वेच्छया कल्पयेद्व्यूहं ज्ञात्वा वा रिपुकल्पितम्॥2.177.30॥
व्यूहे भेदावहं कुर्याद्रिपुव्यूहस्य पार्थिवः ॥
गजस्य देया रक्षार्थं चत्वारस्तु रथा द्विज॥31॥
रथस्य चाश्वाश्चत्वारोऽश्वस्य तस्य च वर्मिणः ॥
वर्मिभिश्च समास्तत्र धन्विनः परिकीर्तिताः॥32॥
पुरस्ताच्चर्मिणो देया देयास्तदनु धन्विनः ॥
धन्विनामनु चाश्वीयं रथांस्तदनु योजयेत् ॥33॥
रथानां कुञ्जराश्चानु दातव्याः पृथिवीक्षिता ॥
पदातिकुञ्जराश्वानां वर्म कार्यं प्रयत्नतः ॥34॥
2.36.m:
He should not arrange the warriors in the array too closely packed or too scattered, / in such a way that there is no clash of weapons among one another.
Such an arrangement of warriors should be made, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / Desiring to break through the enemy's force, he should break it only with dense [units].
Likewise, dense [units] should be formed by one intent on guarding against being broken. / He should form an array according to his own will or after knowing what the enemy has formed.
The king should devise in the array that which brings division to the enemy's array. / Four chariots should be assigned for the protection of an elephant, O twice-born;
and four horses for a chariot, and for a horse, an armoured man; / and bowmen equal [in number] to the armoured men are prescribed there.
Shield-bearers should be placed in front; after them bowmen should be placed; / after the bowmen, cavalry; and after them he should employ chariots.
Elephants should be assigned after chariots by the ruler of the earth. / Armour should be diligently provided for infantry, elephants, and horses.

2.36.s:
avarmayitvā yo vāhaṃ cātmānaṃ varmayennaraḥ ..

2.36.d:
अवर्मयित्वा यो वाहं चात्मानं वर्मयेन्नरः ॥
स राम नरकं याति स्वकृतेनापि कर्मणा ॥ 35 ॥
शूराः प्रमुखतो देया न देया भीरवः क्वचित् ॥
शूरान्वा मुखतो दत्त्वा स्कन्दमात्रप्रदर्शनम् ॥ 36॥
कर्तव्यं भीरुसंघेन शत्रुविद्रावकारकम् ॥
दारयन्ति पुरस्तात्तु विद्रुता भीरवः पुरः ॥ 37 ॥
प्रोत्सारयन्ते वरुणी भीरूञ्शूरान्पुनः स्थिताः ॥
प्रांशवः शुकनासाश्च ये च जिह्वेक्षणा नराः ॥ 38 ॥
संहतभ्रूयुगाश्चैव क्रोधनाः कलहप्रियाः ॥
नित्यं हृष्टाश्च ह्रस्वाश्च शूरा ज्ञेयाश्च कामिनः ॥ 39 ॥
दाक्षिणात्याश्च विज्ञेयाः कुशलाः खड्गवर्मिणः ॥
वङ्कला धान्विनो ज्ञेयाः पार्वतीयास्तथैव च ॥ 2.177.40 ॥
पाषाणयुद्धकुशलास्तथा पर्वतवासिनः ॥
पांचालाः शूरसेनाश्च रथेषु कुशला नराः ॥ 41॥
2.36.m:
The man who, without armouring his mount, arms himself, / goes to hell by his own deed, O Rāma.
Warriors of valour should be placed at the forefront; cowards should never be placed there. / Or, having placed warriors at the head, merely a display of an army's bulk
should be made with a multitude of cowards, causing the enemy to flee. / But in the front, fleeing cowards tear through [their own ranks] ahead.
Firmly stationed, they repel the cowards [and encourage] the brave once more. / Men who are tall, have parrot-like noses, and have squinting eyes,
and whose eyebrows meet, who are prone to anger and fond of strife, / always cheerful, short in stature, and lustful, should be known as brave.
Southerners should be known as skilled sword-and-shield fighters; / the Vaṅkalas should be known as archers, and likewise the mountaineers;
the mountain-dwellers are also skilled in stone-fighting. / The men of Pañcāla and Śūrasena are skilled in chariots;

2.36.s:
kāmbojā ye ca gāṃdhārāḥ kuśalāste hayeṣu ca ..
prāyaśaśca tathā mlecchā vijñeyāḥ pāśayodhinaḥ .. 42 ..
aṅgā vaṅgā kaliṅgāśca jñeyā mātaṅgayodhinaḥ ..
āhatānāṃ hatānāṃ ca raṇāpanayanakriyā .. 43 ..

2.36.d:
काम्बोजा ये च गांधाराः कुशलास्ते हयेषु च ॥
प्रायशश्च तथा म्लेच्छा विज्ञेयाः पाशयोधिनः ॥ 42 ॥
अङ्गा वङ्गा कलिङ्गाश्च ज्ञेया मातङ्गयोधिनः ॥
आहतानां हतानां च रणापनयनक्रिया ॥ 43 ॥
पत्तियोधगजानाञ्च तोयदानादिकं च यत् ॥
आयुधानयनं चैव पत्तिकर्म विधीयते ॥ ॥ 44 ॥
रिपूणां भेदकामानां स्वसैन्यस्य तु रक्षणम् ॥
भेदनं संहतानां च कर्मणां चर्म कीर्तितम् ॥ 45 ॥
विमुखीकरणं युद्धे धन्विनां च तथोच्यते ॥
चर्मिभिः क्रियते शूरैर्भिन्नानामपि संहतिः ॥ 46 ॥
शूरापसरणं यावत्साश्वीयस्य तथोच्यते ॥
त्रासने रिपुसैन्यानां रथकर्म तथोच्यते ॥ 47 ॥
प्राकारगोमुखाट्टालद्रुमभंगाश्च भार्गव ॥
गजानां कर्म निर्दिष्टं यदसह्यं तथा परैः ॥ 48॥
पत्तिभूविषमाजेया रथाश्वस्य तथा समा॥
शर्माद्रुमा च नागानां युद्धभूमिरुदाहृता ॥ 49 ॥
2.36.m:
those of Kamboja and Gāndhāra are skilled on horses; / and generally the mlecchas are to be known as snare-fighters;
the Aṅgas, Vaṅgas, and Kaliṅgas are to be known as elephant-fighters. / The task of carrying the wounded and the slain from the battlefield,
the giving of water and the like to foot-soldiers and elephants, / and the fetching of weapons is prescribed as the work of the infantry.
The protection of one's own army against enemies wishing to divide it, / and the piercing of dense [ranks] is proclaimed as the work of the shield-bearer.
Turning the bowmen around in battle is also thus spoken of. / The rallying even of broken [troops] is accomplished by heroic shield-bearers.
As far as the retreat of the brave is concerned, that is spoken of as belonging to the cavalry; / the terrifying of enemy armies is spoken of as the work of the chariot.
The demolition of ramparts, gates, towers, and trees, O descendant of Bhṛgu, / which is unbearable to enemies, is designated as the work of elephants.
Uneven ground is to be known as that of infantry, and even ground as that of chariots and horses; / ground with soft soil and trees is declared the battleground for elephants.

śakunā maṅgalāścaiva dṛśyante hi mano'nugā.. .. 53 ..

2.36.d:
एवं विरचितव्यूहः कृतपृष्ठदिवाकरः ॥
तथानुलोमशुक्रो वा दिक्पालबुधमारुताः ॥ 2.177.50 ॥
योधानुत्तेजयेत्सर्वान्रामगोत्रापदाननः ॥
भोगप्राप्तिश्च विजये स्वर्गप्राप्तिर्मृतस्य च ॥ 51 ॥
धन्यानि तु निमित्तानि वदन्ति विजयं द्विज ॥
स्पन्दनं शुभगात्राणां शुभस्वप्ननिदर्शनम् ॥ 52 ॥
निमित्तं च गजाश्वस्य सर्वतो दृश्यते शुभम् ॥
शकुना मङ्गलाश्चैव दृश्यन्ते हि मनोऽनुगा॥ ॥ 53 ॥
विपरीतसरीसर्पान्मृत्युः स्पृशति नान्यथा ॥
भवन्तोऽपि कुले जाताः सर्वशस्त्रास्त्रपारगाः ॥ 54 ॥
गान्धर्वे च परा नित्यं नित्यं सन्मार्गमाश्रिताः ॥
अनाहार्याः परैर्नित्यं कथं न स्याज्जयो मम ॥ 55 ॥
राजश्रीर्भवतामेव भवद्भिः केवलं मम ॥
द्वे चामरेऽधिके शूराच्छत्रं चर्माभमेव च ॥ 56 ॥
2.36.m:
Having thus arranged the battle array, with the sun behind his back, / or likewise with Venus in his favour, as well as the guardians of the directions, Mercury, and the wind,
he should encourage all the warriors, O Rāma, by their lineage and past deeds: / 'There is the attainment of enjoyment in victory, and attainment of heaven for the slain!
Auspicious omens declare victory, O twice-born: / the throbbing of auspicious limbs, the seeing of auspicious dreams,
and auspicious signs of elephants and horses are seen on every side; / indeed, omens and auspicious birds are seen agreeable to the mind!
Death touches only the contrary crawlers [on the ground], not otherwise! / You also are born of good family, masters of all weapons and missiles,
always devoted to noble conduct, always adhering to the right path, / never corruptible by enemies; how could victory not be mine?
The majesty of royalty is yours alone, and mine is solely through you. / Only two chowries and a parasol, resembling a shield, are superior [as royal marks], O warriors!

2.36.s:
jitvarīnbhogasaṃprāptirmṛtasya ca parā gatiḥ ..
niṣkṛtiḥ svāmipiṇḍasya nāsti yuddhasamā gatiḥ .. 57 ..
śūrāṇāṃ yadviniryāti raktamābādhataḥ kvacit ..
tenaiva saha pāpmānaṃ sarva tyajati dhārmika .. 58 ..
tathā bādhacikitsāyāṃ vedanāsahite tathā ..
tato nāstyadhikaṃ loke kiñcitparamadāruṇam .. 59 ..
mṛtasya nāgnisaṃskāro nāśaucannodakakriyā ..
kartumicchati yasyeha saṃgrāmādadhikaṃ nu kim .. 2.177.60 ..
2.36.d:
जित्वरीन्भोगसंप्राप्तिर्मृतस्य च परा गतिः ॥
निष्कृतिः स्वामिपिण्डस्य नास्ति युद्धसमा गतिः ॥ 57 ॥
शूराणां यद्विनिर्याति रक्तमाबाधतः क्वचित् ॥
तेनैव सह पाप्मानं सर्व त्यजति धार्मिक ॥ 58 ॥
तथा बाधचिकित्सायां वेदनासहिते तथा ॥
ततो नास्त्यधिकं लोके किञ्चित्परमदारुणम् ॥ 59 ॥
मृतस्य नाग्निसंस्कारो नाशौचन्नोदकक्रिया ॥
कर्तुमिच्छति यस्येह संग्रामादधिकं नु किम् ॥ 2.177.60 ॥
2.36.m:
To the victors belongs the attainment of enjoyment, and to the slain the highest destination. / Discharging the master's bread [has no equal]; there is no state equal to battle!
Whatever blood issues forth from the wound of warriors anywhere, / with that alone he casts off all sin, O righteous one!
Likewise, in the treatment of wounds, when accompanied by intense pain, / there is nothing greater or more terrible in the world than that.
For the slain there is no cremation rite, no ritual impurity, and no water-offering; / for one who wishes to make [an offering], what indeed is greater in this world than battle?

2.36.s:
tapasvino dānaparā yajvāno bahudakṣiṇāḥ ..
śūrāṇāṃ gatimicchanti dṛṣṭvā bhogānanuttamān ..61 ..
2.36.d:
तपस्विनो दानपरा यज्वानो बहुदक्षिणाः ॥
शूराणां गतिमिच्छन्ति दृष्ट्वा भोगाननुत्तमान् ॥61 ॥
2.36.m: Ascetics, the generous, and sacrificers who give lavish sacrificial fees / desire the destiny of heroes upon seeing their unsurpassed enjoyments.

2.36.s:
varāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi śūramāyodhane hatam ..
abhidravanti kāmārtā mama bhartā bhaviṣyati .. 62 ..
2.36.d:
वराप्सरःसहस्राणि शूरमायोधने हतम् ॥
अभिद्रवन्ति कामार्ता मम भर्ता भविष्यति ॥ 62 ॥
2.36.m: Thousands of foremost apsarases rush toward a hero slain in battle, / afflicted with longing: "He shall be my husband!"

2.36.s:
svāmī sukṛtamādatte bhagnānāṃ vinivartatām ..
brahmahatyāphalaṃ teṣāṃ tathā proktaṃ padepade .. 63 ..
2.36.d:
स्वामी सुकृतमादत्ते भग्नानां विनिवर्तताम् ॥
ब्रह्महत्याफलं तेषां तथा प्रोक्तं पदेपदे ॥ 63 ॥
2.36.m: The master takes the good karma of those who are routed and turn back; / the fruit of killing a brahmin is proclaimed for them at every step.

2.36.s:
yaḥ sahāyānparityajya svastimāngantumicchati ..
asvasti tasya kurvanti devāḥ śakrapurogamāḥ .. 64 ..
2.36.d:
यः सहायान्परित्यज्य स्वस्तिमान्गन्तुमिच्छति ॥
अस्वस्ति तस्य कुर्वन्ति देवाः शक्रपुरोगमाः ॥ 64 ॥
2.36.m: He who, abandoning his companions, wishes to escape safely, / the gods headed by Śakra bring misfortune upon him.

2.36.s:
aśvamedhaphalaṃ proktaṃ bhagnānāmanivartatām ..
padepade mahābhāgā saṃmukhānāṃ mahātmanām .. 65 ..
2.36.d:
अश्वमेधफलं प्रोक्तं भग्नानामनिवर्तताम् ॥
पदेपदे महाभागा संमुखानां महात्मनाम् ॥ 65 ॥
2.36.m: The fruit of the horse sacrifice is declared at every step, O fortunate one, / for those who are broken but do not turn back, confronting [the enemy], noble in spirit.

2.36.s:
devastriyastathā lakṣmīḥ pāpmānamayaśastathā ..
pratīkṣante mahābhāga saṃgrāme samupasthite .. 66 ..
2.36.d:
देवस्त्रियस्तथा लक्ष्मीः पाप्मानमयशस्तथा ॥
प्रतीक्षन्ते महाभाग संग्रामे समुपस्थिते ॥ 66 ॥
2.36.m: Celestial women and fortune, as well as sin and dishonour, / await, O fortunate one, when battle is at hand.'

2.36.s:
parāṅmukhā mayā grāhyā jīvantopyabhavā mṛtāḥ ..
ityevamayaśastasya pāpmanā saha tiṣṭhati .. 67 ..
2.36.d:
पराङ्मुखा मया ग्राह्या जीवन्तोप्यभवा मृताः ॥
इत्येवमयशस्तस्य पाप्मना सह तिष्ठति ॥ 67 ॥
2.36.m: "Those who turn their backs are to be seized by me; whether living or dead, they have no future." / In this way disgrace stands along with sin for him.

2.36.s: lakṣmīḥ santiṣṭhate tasya jīvataḥ kṛtakarmaṇaḥ .. 68 ..
2.36.d: लक्ष्मीः सन्तिष्ठते तस्य जीवतः कृतकर्मणः ॥ 68 ॥
2.36.m: Fortune abides with him who is alive and has done his duty;

2.36.s:
mṛtasya cāpi tiṣṭhanti vimānasthā surastriyaḥ ..
evamudghoṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā dharmeṇecchejjayaṃ raṇe .. 69 ..
2.36.d:
मृतस्य चापि तिष्ठन्ति विमानस्था सुरस्त्रियः ॥
एवमुद्घोषणं कृत्वा धर्मेणेच्छेज्जयं रणे ॥ 69 ॥
2.36.m: and for him who is dead, celestial women seated in aerial chariots await. / Having made such a proclamation, he should desire victory in battle according to dharma.

2.36.s:
adharmavijayo rājño nṛpaloke bhayāvahaḥ ..
adharmavijayādarthairyacchidramupadhīyate .. 2.177.70 ..
2.36.d:
अधर्मविजयो राज्ञो नृपलोके भयावहः ॥
अधर्मविजयादर्थैर्यच्छिद्रमुपधीयते ॥ 2.177.70 ॥
2.36.m: A king's victory through adharma brings terror to the world of kings. / Whatever gap is covered by wealth gained from victory through adharma,

2.36.s:
chidrādeva paraṃ chidraṃ tasya syānnātra saṃśayaḥ ..
na karṇī na tathā digdhaḥ śaraḥ syāddharmayodhinām .. 71 ..
2.36.d:
छिद्रादेव परं छिद्रं तस्य स्यान्नात्र संशयः ॥
न कर्णी न तथा दिग्धः शरः स्याद्धर्मयोधिनाम् ॥ 71 ॥
2.36.m: a greater gap indeed arises from that very gap; of this there is no doubt. / An arrow should not be barbed, nor poisoned, for those who fight according to dharma.

2.36.s:
nāsthiśalyaḥ śaraḥ kāryo dāruśalyaśca bhārgava ..
samaḥ samena yoddhavyo nāpacāro raṇe dvija .. 72 ..
2.36.d:
नास्थिशल्यः शरः कार्यो दारुशल्यश्च भार्गव ॥
समः समेन योद्धव्यो नापचारो रणे द्विज ॥ 72 ॥
2.36.m: An arrow should not have a bone tip, nor a wooden tip, O descendant of Bhṛgu. / An equal should fight with an equal; there must be no transgression in battle, O twice-born.

2.36.s:
sannaddhena ca sannaddhaḥ sāśvaścāśvagatena tu ..
rathī ca rathinā rāma padātiśca padātinā .. 73 ..
2.36.d:
सन्नद्धेन च सन्नद्धः साश्वश्चाश्वगतेन तु ॥
रथी च रथिना राम पदातिश्च पदातिना ॥ 73 ॥
2.36.m: An armored man [should fight] with an armored man, and a horseman with one mounted on a horse; / a charioteer with a charioteer, O Rāma, and a foot-soldier with a foot-soldier.

2.36.s:
kuñjarastho gajasthena yoddhavyo bhṛgunandana ..
vimukho bhagnaśastraśca strībālaparirakṣitā .. 74 ..
2.36.d:
कुञ्जरस्थो गजस्थेन योद्धव्यो भृगुनन्दन ॥
विमुखो भग्नशस्त्रश्च स्त्रीबालपरिरक्षिता ॥ 74 ॥
2.36.m: One mounted on an elephant should fight with one on an elephant, O scion of Bhṛgu. / One whose back is turned, one whose weapon is broken, one protecting women and children,

2.36.s:
vyāyudho bhagnagātraśca tathaiva śaraṇāgataḥ ..
pareṇa yuddhyamānaśca yuddhaprekṣaka eva ca .. 75 ..
2.36.d:
व्यायुधो भग्नगात्रश्च तथैव शरणागतः ॥
परेण युद्ध्यमानश्च युद्धप्रेक्षक एव च ॥ 75 ॥
2.36.m: one who has laid down weapons, one whose limbs are broken, and likewise one who has sought refuge, / one fighting with another, and a spectator of the battle,

2.36.s:
ārtastoyapradātā ca daṇḍapāṇistathaiva ca ..
ete raṇe na hantavyā kṣatradharmamabhīpsatā .. 76 ..
2.36.d:
आर्तस्तोयप्रदाता च दण्डपाणिस्तथैव च ॥
एते रणे न हन्तव्या क्षत्रधर्ममभीप्सता ॥ 76 ॥
2.36.m: a distressed person, a water-giver, and likewise one who holds only a staff— / these must not be slain in battle by one who desires the kṣatriya dharma.

2.36.s:
pāpiṣṭho kūṭayuddhe ca kartavyamapi cāhave ..
śrāntena vābhibhūtena ardhottīrṇabalena ca .. 77 ..
2.36.d:
पापिष्ठो कूटयुद्धे च कर्तव्यमपि चाहवे ॥
श्रान्तेन वाभिभूतेन अर्धोत्तीर्णबलेन च ॥ 77 ॥
2.36.m: The most wicked [deed] must be done in deceptive warfare and in combat / against one who is exhausted, overcome, or whose army has only half-crossed [a river].

2.36.s: durdine na ca yuddhāni kartavyāni mahābala .. 78 ..
2.36.d: दुर्दिने न च युद्धानि कर्तव्यानि महाबल ॥ 78 ॥
2.36.m: And battles should not be fought on a bad day, O mighty one.

2.36.s:
pravṛtte samare rāma pareṣāṃ nāmakāraṇāt ..
bāhū pragṛhya vikrośedbhagnā bhagnāḥ pare tviti ..
prāptaṃ mitrabalaṃ bhūri nāyako'tra nipātitaḥ .. 79 ..
2.36.d:
प्रवृत्ते समरे राम परेषां नामकारणात् ॥
बाहू प्रगृह्य विक्रोशेद्भग्ना भग्नाः परे त्विति ॥
प्राप्तं मित्रबलं भूरि नायकोऽत्र निपातितः ॥ 79 ॥
2.36.m: When the battle has begun, O Rāma, for the purpose of [demoralizing] the enemies, / holding up both arms he should shout: "Broken, the enemies are broken! / An abundant allied force has arrived! The leader here is struck down!

2.36.s:
senānīrnihataścāyaṃ sarvā senāpi vidrutā ..
evaṃ citrāsanaṃ kuryātpareṣāṃ bhṛgunandana .. 2.177.80 ..
2.36.d:
सेनानीर्निहतश्चायं सर्वा सेनापि विद्रुता ॥
एवं चित्रासनं कुर्यात्परेषां भृगुनन्दन ॥ 2.177.80 ॥
2.36.m: This army commander is slain! The entire army has fled!" / In this way, O scion of Bhṛgu, one should cause dismay among the enemies.

2.36.s:
vidrutānāṃ tu yodhānāṃ suvighāto vidhīyate ..
dhanurvedavidhānena kalpanā ca tathā bhavet .. 81 ..
2.36.d:
विद्रुतानां तु योधानां सुविघातो विधीयते ॥
धनुर्वेदविधानेन कल्पना च तथा भवेत् ॥ 81 ॥
2.36.m: A successful pursuit of fleeing warriors is prescribed; / and an arrangement should be made according to the rules of the Dhanurveda.

2.36.s:
pāpāśca deyā dharmajña tathaiva paramohanāḥ ..
patākābhyucchrayaḥ kāryaḥ svabale ca tathā śubhaḥ .. 82 ..
2.36.d:
पापाश्च देया धर्मज्ञ तथैव परमोहनाः ॥
पताकाभ्युच्छ्रयः कार्यः स्वबले च तथा शुभः ॥ 82 ॥
2.36.m: And wicked [tricks] should be used, O knower of dharma, which cause extreme confusion. / An auspicious raising of banners should be done among one's own troops,

2.36.s:
saṃskāraścaiva kartavyo vāditrāṇāṃ bhayāvahaḥ ..
etasya varṣaṃ vakṣyāmi tavopaniṣadi dvija .. 83 ..
2.36.d:
संस्कारश्चैव कर्तव्यो वादित्राणां भयावहः ॥
एतस्य वर्षं वक्ष्यामि तवोपनिषदि द्विज ॥ 83 ॥
2.36.m: and terrifying preparation of musical instruments should be made. / I shall declare its verse to you in the secret teaching, O twice-born.

2.36.s:
saṃprāpya vijayaṃ yuddhe kāryaṃ daivatapūjanam ..
pūjayedbrāhmaṇāṃścātra gurūnapi ca pūjayet .. 84 ..
2.36.d:
संप्राप्य विजयं युद्धे कार्यं दैवतपूजनम् ॥
पूजयेद्ब्राह्मणांश्चात्र गुरूनपि च पूजयेत् ॥ 84 ॥
2.36.m: Having obtained victory in battle, worship of the deities must be performed; / one should worship the brahmins there, and also worship the elders.

2.36.s:
ratnāni rājagāmīni carma vāhanamāyudham ..
sarvamanyadbhavettasya yadyenaiva raṇe hṛtam .. 85 ..
2.36.d:
रत्नानि राजगामीनि चर्म वाहनमायुधम् ॥
सर्वमन्यद्भवेत्तस्य यद्येनैव रणे हृतम् ॥ 85 ॥
2.36.m: Gems go to the king, as do shields, mounts, and weapons; / everything else belongs to him by whom it was seized in battle.

2.36.s:
kulastriyastu vijñeyāstathā rāma na kasyacit ..
svadeśe paradeśe vā sādhvīṃ yatnānna dūṣayet .. 86 ..
2.36.d:
कुलस्त्रियस्तु विज्ञेयास्तथा राम न कस्यचित् ॥
स्वदेशे परदेशे वा साध्वीं यत्नान्न दूषयेत् ॥ 86 ॥
2.36.m: Women of noble family, however, O Rāma, should be known as belonging to no one; / in one's own country or in a foreign country, one should not dishonor a virtuous woman with effort.

2.36.s:
anyathā saṃkaro ghoro bhavatīha kṣayāvahaḥ ..
śakraḥ prāpya raṇe muktaḥ putrastasya prakīrtitaḥ .. 87 ..
2.36.d:
अन्यथा संकरो घोरो भवतीह क्षयावहः ॥
शक्रः प्राप्य रणे मुक्तः पुत्रस्तस्य प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 87 ॥
2.36.m: Otherwise, a terrible mixture [of castes] arises here, which brings ruin. / Śakra, captured in battle, was released; his son is proclaimed [as an example].

2.36.s:
purastenāsya yoddhavyaṃ tasya dharmaṃ vijānatā ..
deśedeśe ya ācāraḥ pāramparyakramāgataḥ .. 88 ..
2.36.d:
पुरस्तेनास्य योद्धव्यं तस्य धर्मं विजानता ॥
देशेदेशे य आचारः पारम्पर्यक्रमागतः ॥ 88 ॥
2.36.m: One who knows dharma should fight in front of him. / Whatever custom exists in each country, handed down through tradition,

2.36.s:
sa eva paripālyaḥ syātprāpya deśaṃ mahīkṣitā ..
nṛṇāṃ pradarśayedrājā samare'pi hate ripau .. 89 ..
2.36.d:
स एव परिपाल्यः स्यात्प्राप्य देशं महीक्षिता ॥
नृणां प्रदर्शयेद्राजा समरेऽपि हते रिपौ ॥ 89 ॥
2.36.m: that very [custom] should be protected by the ruler of the earth upon acquiring the land. / Even when the enemy is slain in battle, the king should show to the people:

2.36.s:
na me priyaṃ kṛtaṃ tena yenāyaṃ samare hataḥ ..
kintu pūjā karomyasya svacchandamavijānataḥ .. 2.177.90 ..
2.36.d:
न मे प्रियं कृतं तेन येनायं समरे हतः ॥
किन्तु पूजा करोम्यस्य स्वच्छन्दमविजानतः ॥ 2.177.90 ॥
2.36.m: "Nothing pleasing was done for me by him by whom this [foe] was killed in battle. / Yet I show honor to him who did not know my wish;

2.36.s:
hato'yaṃ maddhitārthāya priyaṃ yadyapi no mama ..
aputrāśca striyaścaiva nṛpatiḥ paripālayet .. 91 ..
2.36.d:

2.178
राम उवाच ॥
धनुर्वेदं समाचक्ष्व संक्षेपात्सुरनन्दन ॥
सर्वं त्वमेव जानासि यथा देवः पितामहः ॥ ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
चतुष्पादो धनुर्वेदस्तथा पञ्चविधो द्विज ॥
रथनागाश्वपत्तीनां पादानाश्रित्य कीर्तितः ॥ 2 ॥
यन्त्रमुक्तं प्राणिमुक्तं मुक्तसन्धारितं तथा ॥
अमुक्तं बाहुयुद्धं च पञ्चधा तत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 3 ॥
तच्च शस्त्रास्त्रसंपत्त्या द्विविधं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
दण्डमायाविभेदेन भूयो द्विविधमुच्यते ॥
ऋजुमायाविभेदेन भूयो द्विविधमुच्यते ॥ 4 ॥
क्षेपणीचापयन्त्राद्यं यन्त्रमुक्तं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 5 ॥
शिलातोमरचक्राद्यं पाणिमुक्तं तथैव च ॥
मुक्तसन्धारितं ज्ञेयं पाशाद्यमपि यद्भवेत् ॥ 6 ॥
2.36.m:
Having acquired the earth through dharma, marked with gardens, sacrificial posts, and temples of the gods, / and having given other [lands] according to his ability to twice-born men, [the subjects] conquer the world for this lord of men.
Rāma said: / Explain the Dhanurveda in brief, O delight of the gods; / you know everything, just like the divine Grandfather.
Puṣkara said: / The Dhanurveda has four quarters and five divisions, O twice-born, / proclaimed as resting on the quarters of chariots, elephants, horses, and foot-soldiers.
Discharged from machines, discharged by hand, discharged and retained, / unreleased, and hand-to-hand combat—thus it is declared to be fivefold.
And that is declared to be twofold through the attainment of weapons and missiles; / it is further said to be twofold by the distinction of force and deceit; / it is further said to be twofold by the distinction of straightforward and deceptive [methods].
Sling, bow, machine, and the like are declared to be discharged from machines.
A stone, a javelin, a discus, and the like are discharged by hand; / that which is a noose and the like should be known as discharged and retained.

2.36.d:
खड्गादिकमनुक्तं च तथा ज्ञेयं महाभुज ॥
नियुद्धं व्यायुधं ज्ञेयं पाणिप्रहरणादिकम् ॥ 7 ॥
तत्रादावेव योग्यत्वं गात्राणां तु विधीयते ॥
तथा व्यायामचारित्वं भारकर्षणमेव च ॥ 8 ॥
जितश्रमो हि युद्धेषु कर्मयोग्यत्वमाप्नुयात् ॥
रथाश्वगजपृष्ठेषु तानि शस्त्राणि चाभ्यसेत्॥॥
तानि वै खड्गमुख्यानि बाहुप्रत्यवराणि च॥
धनुर्वेदे गुरुर्विप्रः प्रोक्तो वर्णद्वयस्य च॥2.178.10॥
वैश्यस्य गुरुतां कुर्यान्न वा कुर्यात्तथा द्विजम् ॥
धनुर्वेदे न गुरुतां शूद्रः कुर्यात्कदाचन ॥ 11 ॥
स्वयमेव तु शूद्रं च कर्तव्या कर्मयोग्यता ॥
तस्मायुद्धाधिकारोस्ति शूद्रस्यापि विशांपते ॥ 12 ॥
सङ्गराणामपि तथा हितः स्यात्स स्वयं प्रभोः ॥
सर्वरत्नैर्महाराज राजा रक्ष्यः प्रयत्नतः ॥ 13 ॥
2.36.m:
The sword and the like should be known as unreleased, O mighty-armed one. / Unarmed close combat should be known as fighting with fists and the like.
In that regard, fitness of the limbs is prescribed at the very beginning, / as well as practice of exercise and pulling loads.
For he who has conquered fatigue will attain fitness for action in battles. / And he should practice those weapons on the backs of chariots, horses, and elephants; / they have swords as the chief and hands as the lowest. / In the Dhanurveda, an inspired teacher is declared to be the teacher for the two [upper] classes.
A twice-born may or may not act as teacher to a vaiśya; / a śūdra should never act as a teacher in the Dhanurveda.
Fitness for action should be acquired by a śūdra by himself; / therefore, even a śūdra has the qualification for fighting, O lord of the people.
He should also be beneficial in battles for his master by himself. / A king should be protected with effort by means of all precious things, O great king.

2.179
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
पाणिपादतले पृष्ठं सर्वे स्युः संहिता यदि ॥
दृष्टं सामपदं स्थानमेतल्लक्षणतस्तधा ॥ 1 ॥
बाह्यांगुलिः स्फिचौ पादौ स्तब्धजानुबलावुभौ ॥
त्रिवितस्त्यन्तरायाममेवं वैशाखमुच्यते ॥ 2 ॥
मण्डलाकारपादाभ्यामुद्यते यत्र जानुनी ॥
चतुर्विधं त्रिविच्छिन्नं तदेवं मण्डलं स्मृतम् ॥3॥
फलाकृतिसमं यच्च स्तब्धजानूरुदक्षिणम्॥
वितस्तिपञ्चविस्तारन्तदालीढं प्रकीर्तितम्॥4॥
नमिता पूर्वजङ्घा च सदालीढविधीयते॥
तिर्यग्गतो भवेद्वामो दक्षिणोऽपि भवेदृजुः ॥ 5॥
गुल्फौ पार्णिस्थितावेव स्थिरौ पञ्चाङ्गुलान्तरौ ॥
स्थानजातं भवेदेतद्द्वादशाङ्गुलमायतम् ॥ 6 ॥
2.36.m:
The good say that those to be taught are faithful, devoted, well-behaved, humble, disciplined, endowed with patience, / affectionate, rulers of men, very firm, and pleasing.
2.179
Puṣkara said:
If both the palms, soles of the feet, and the back are aligned,
this stance is seen as sāmapada, according to its characteristics.
With the toes turned outwards, the buttocks [tucked], both feet with knees stiff and firm, / and an interval of three spans—thus the vaiśākha stance is described.
Where both knees are raised with feet forming a circle, / divided into four kinds and separated by three [spans], that is known as the maṇḍala stance.
That which resembles an arrowhead, with the right knee and thigh held rigid, / and five spans in breadth, is celebrated as the ālīḍha stance.
The forward shank bent is always prescribed for the ālīḍha;
the left [foot] should be placed transversely, and the right should be straight.
The two ankles firmly resting on the heels, separated by five fingers' width—
this posture is twelve fingers in length.

2.36.d:
एतदेव विपर्यस्तं प्रत्याख्यातं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
कुब्जजानुर्भवेद्वामो दक्षिणस्तु प्रसारितः ॥7॥
अथ वा दक्षिणं जानुं कुब्जं भवति निश्चलम् ॥
भवेद्दण्डायतो वामश्चरणः सह जानुना ॥ 8 ॥
एवं विकच्छमुद्दिष्टं द्विहस्तान्तरमायतम् ॥
जानुनी द्विगुणौ स्यातां ह्युत्तानौ चरणावपि ॥ 9 ॥
अनेन विनियोगेन सम्पुटं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
किञ्चिद्विवर्तितौ पादौ समदण्डायतौ स्थिरौ ॥ 2.179.10 ॥
दृष्टिमेव यथान्यायं षोडशाङ्गुलमायतम् ॥
स्वस्तिकेनात्र कुर्वीत प्रणामं प्रथमं द्विजः ॥ 11 ॥
कार्मुकं भृगुवामेन वामं दक्षिणकेन वा ॥
वैशाखेप्यथ वा जाते स्थितो वा प्यथ वायते ॥ 12 ॥
गुणाग्रं तु ततः कृत्वा कार्मुके प्रियकार्मुकः॥
अधःकोटिं तु धनुषः फलदेशे च पत्रिणः ॥13॥
2.36.m:
This very [posture] reversed is proclaimed as pratyālīḍha:
the left knee should be bent, while the right is stretched out.
Or, the right knee becomes bent and motionless, / and the left foot, together with the knee, should be extended like a staff.
Thus the vikaccha is prescribed, extending over a distance of two cubits; / the knees should be twice [bent], and the feet upturned.
By this application, the sampuṭa stance is proclaimed:
the feet slightly turned, extended straight like a staff, and firm.
The gaze should be sixteen fingers long, in accordance with the rules.
First, the twice-born should make a salutation with crossed hands.
O descendant of Bhṛgu, [holding] the bow with the left hand, or the left with the right,
standing either in the vaiśākha stance or in the extended stance,
the lover of the bow, having then fixed the tip of the bowstring onto the bow, / should place the lower tip of the bow and the feathered arrow at its head,

2.36.d:
धरण्यां स्थापयित्वा तु लालयित्वा तथैव च॥
भुजाभ्यामत्र कुब्जाभ्यां प्रकोष्ठाभ्यामरिंदम॥14॥
न्यस्य बाणं धनुःश्रेष्ठं पुङ्खदेशे च पत्रिणः ॥
विन्यासो धनुषश्चैव द्वादशाङ्गुलमन्तरः॥15॥
तयोर्भार्गव कर्तव्यो नातो हीनो न चाधिकः ॥
निवेश्य कार्मुकं कण्ठे नितम्बे शरसङ्करम्॥16.
उत्क्षिपेदस्थिरंहस्तमन्तरेणाक्षिकर्णयोः ॥
पूर्वेण मुष्टिना ग्राह्यः स्तनाग्रं दक्षिणः शरः ॥ 17 ॥
हरणं तु ततः कृत्वा शीघ्रं पूर्वां प्रसारयेत्॥
नात्यन्तरा नैव बाह्या नोर्ध्वगा नाधरास्तथा ॥ 18 ॥
न च कुब्जा न चोत्ताना न चला नातिवेष्टिताः ॥
समाः स्थैर्यगुणोपेताः पूर्वे दण्डमिव स्थिताः ॥ 19 ॥
छादयित्वा ततो लक्ष्यं पूर्वेणानेन मुष्टिना ॥
तरसा तूत्थितो यत्नात्त्रिकोणविनतिस्थितः ॥2.179.20॥
2.36.m:
and having rested it on the ground and likewise caressed it, / with both arms bent and forearms [ready], O subduer of foes,
having placed the arrow on the excellent bow and on the nock of the feathered shaft, / the interval between the placements of the bow should be twelve fingers.
Between the two, O Bhārgava, it must be made neither less nor more.
Having placed the bow at the throat, and the quiver of arrows at the hip,
one should raise the unsteady hand between the eye and the ear.
The front fist must grasp the arrow, the right one at the nipple's tip.
Then, having drawn it back, one should quickly stretch forward the front [hand];
neither too internal nor external, neither raised up nor lowered,
neither bent nor upturned, neither trembling nor excessively twisted, / level, endowed with the quality of firmness, standing like a staff in front.
Then, having covered the target with this front fist, / swiftly rising with effort, standing inclined in a triangle,

tṛtīye'ṅgulamuddiṣṭaṃ cāyataṃ cibukāṃsayoḥ ..
gṛhītvā sāyakaṃ tatra tarjanyaṅguṣṭhameva ca .. 23 ..

2.36.d:
स्रस्तांसो निश्चलग्रीवो मयूरांचितमस्तकः ॥
ललाटनासावक्त्रांसः कूर्परश्च समं भवेत् ॥ 21 ॥
अन्तरं त्वङ्गुलं ज्ञेयं चिबुकस्यांसकस्य च ॥
प्रथमे त्र्यङ्गुले विन्द्याद्द्वितीये द्व्यङ्गुलं स्मृतम् ॥ 22॥
तृतीयेऽङ्गुलमुद्दिष्टं चायतं चिबुकांसयोः ॥
गृहीत्वा सायकं तत्र तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठमेव च ॥ 23 ॥
अनामया ततो गृह्य पुनर्मध्यमयापि च ॥
तावदाकर्षयेद्योगाद्यावद्बाणः सुपूरितः ॥ 24 ॥।
एवंविधमुपक्रम्य मोक्तव्यो विधिवत्खगः ॥
दृष्टिमुष्टिहतं लक्ष्यं भिन्द्याद्बाणेन भार्गव॥25॥
मुक्त्वा चापं वामहस्तं क्षिपेद्वेगेन पृच्छतः ॥
एतदुच्छेदमिच्छन्ति ज्ञातव्यं हि त्वया द्विज ॥ 26 ॥
कूर्परं त्रिविधं कार्यमाकृष्टन्तु धनुष्मता ॥
तत्रापि मुक्तके कार्यमक्षश्लिष्टस्तु मध्यमम् ॥ 27 ॥
2.36.m:
with drooping shoulders, motionless neck, head arched like a peacock's, / the forehead, nose, face, shoulder, and elbow should be level.
The interval between the chin and the shoulder should be known in fingers:
in the first it should be known as three fingers, in the second it is said to be two fingers,
in the third it is prescribed as one finger's length between chin and shoulder.
Grasping the arrow there with the index finger and the thumb,
then holding it with the ring finger and again with the middle finger, / one should draw it with discipline until the arrow is fully pulled.
Having undertaken [this] in such a manner, the flying shaft should be released according to rule.
One should pierce with the arrow the target struck by the gaze and the fist, O Bhārgava.
Having released the bow, one should throw the left hand back with force.
They desire this cutting off; it must indeed be understood by you, O twice-born.
The elbow should be drawn back in three ways by the archer;
even there, when released, it should be made adjoining the eye in the middle drawing.

puṣkara uvāca ..

2.36.d:
ज्येष्ठं प्रकृष्टं विज्ञेयं धनुःशास्त्रविशारदाः ॥
ज्येष्ठस्तु पावको ज्ञेयो भवेद्द्वादशमुष्टयः ॥ 28 ॥
एकादश तथा साध्यः कनीयान्दशमुष्टयः ॥
चतुर्हस्तं धनुःश्रेष्ठं प्रयोगं चास्य मध्यमम् ॥ 29 ॥
कनीयसं त्रयः प्रोक्तं नित्यमेव पदातिना ॥
अश्वे रथे गजे ज्येष्ठं तदेव परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 2.179.30 ॥
तदेव हीनं खलु मध्यमं स्यात्तदेव हीनं च तथा कनीयः ॥
पूर्णायुधस्यैष विधिर्मया ते प्रोक्तः समासाद् भृगुवंशमुख्य ॥31॥
2.180
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
पूर्णायुधो भृतिं कृत्वा ततो मांसैर्गतायुषाम् ॥
वराहमृगमेषाणां माहिषाद्यैस्तथा द्विज ॥ 1 ॥
मुनिधौतं ततः कुर्याद्युग्यं भूपैर्विधानवित् ॥
मृदुसंस्तरणोपेतं मृदु वल्गु च योजयेत् ॥ 2 ॥
ततो वाहं समारुह्य दंशितः सुसमाहितः ॥
तूर्णमारुह्य बध्नीयाद्दृढां कक्षां च दक्षिणाम् ॥3॥
2.36.m:
Those skilled in the science of archery know the eldest as the supreme.
The eldest should be known as Pāvaka, and consists of twelve fist-lengths.
The Sādhya has eleven, and the smallest has ten fist-lengths.
A bow of four cubits is best, and its application is middling.
A bow of three [cubits] is declared as the smallest, always for a foot-soldier;
on a horse, chariot, or elephant, that same [four-cubit bow] is proclaimed as the best.
Lesser than that indeed would be middling, and lesser still the smallest.
This rule for one equipped with weapons has been told to you in brief, O foremost of the Bhrgu lineage.
2.180
Puṣkara said:
Equipped with weapons, having made an offering with the flesh of dead / boars, deer, and sheep, and likewise of buffaloes and the like, O twice-born,
the king, knowing the rituals, should then have the chariot washed by sages;
provided with a soft spread, he should harness soft and charming [steeds].
Then, having mounted the steed, armored and well-concentrated, / having mounted swiftly, he should fasten the right girth securely.

2.36.d:
वैकक्ष्यमपि तच्चापं धारयेद्यन्त्रसंस्थितम् ॥
ततो समुद्धरेद्बाणं ऋणाद्दक्षिणपाणिना ॥ 4 ॥
तज्जवः सहितं सर्वं मध्ये संगृह्य धारयेत् ॥
वामहस्तेन वै कक्ष्याद्धनुस्तस्मात्समुद्धरेत् ॥ 5 ॥
सुनिषण्णमणिर्भूत्वा गुणे पुङ्खं निवेशयेत् ॥
संपीड्य सिंहकर्णेन पुंखेनापि समे दृढम् ॥ 6 ॥
वामकर्णोपरिस्थं च फलं व्यामस्य धारणात् ॥
बलामध्यमया तत्र वामांगुल्या च धारयेत् । 7 ॥
मनोलक्ष्यगतं कृत्वा दृष्टिं च सुविधानवित् ॥
दक्षिणे गात्रभागे तु बलामाशु विमोक्षयेत् ॥ 8 ॥
ललाटपुटसंस्थानं दाणीं लक्ष्ये निवेशयेत् ॥ 9 ॥
आकृष्य ताडयेत्तत्र दण्डकं षोडशांगुलम् ॥
मुक्त्वा बाणं ततः पश्चाद्बलां शिक्षेत्तदातदा ॥ 2.180.10 ॥
विगृह्णीयान्मध्यमया ततोंगुल्या पुनःपुनः ॥
अभिलक्ष्याक्षिपेत्तूणांश्चतुरस्रं च दक्षिणम् ॥ 11 ॥
2.36.m:
He should wear that bow across the chest, placed in a harness.
Then he should draw an arrow with his right hand,
swiftly grasping and holding everything together in the middle.
With the left hand, he should indeed draw the bow from that side.
Having the wrist firmly settled, he should place the nock on the bowstring;
pressing firmly with the lion's ear grip, level with the nock,
with the arrowhead resting above the left ear from holding it an arm-span wide,
he should hold the string with the middle and the left finger.
Having directed his mind and his gaze onto the target, knowing the ritual well,
he should quickly release the string on the right side of the body.
Positioned at the hollow of the forehead, he should direct the arrow at the target.
Having drawn back, he should strike the sixteen-finger rod there;
having released the arrow, he should then practice with the bowstring from time to time.
He should grasp [the string] with the middle finger again and again;
aiming at the target, he should shoot arrows, [whether standing] square or on the right.

2.36.d:
चतुरस्रगतं वैध्यमभ्यसेदादितः स्थितः ॥
तस्मादनन्तरं तीक्ष्णं परावृत्तगतं च यत् ॥ 12 ॥
निश्रमुन्नतवेद्यन्तमभ्यसेत्तुष्यकं ततः ॥
वेध्यस्थानेष्वथैतेषु सन्यस्तपुटकं धनुः ॥ 13 ॥
हस्तावापगतैः स्रस्तैर्जपेद्धस्तकरैरपि ॥
तस्मिन्वेध्यगते राम द्वे वेध्ये दृढसंज्ञिते ॥ 14 ॥
द्वे वेध्ये पुष्करे विद्धि द्वे तथा चित्रपुष्करे ॥
चतुरस्रं च तीक्ष्णं च दृढवेध्ये प्रकीर्तिते ॥ 15 ॥
चतुरस्रं स्थूलतीक्ष्णं॥॥॥ ॥
निम्नं पुष्करमुद्दिष्टं वेध्यमूदूर्ध्वगतं च यत् ॥ 16 ॥
पुष्करेऽधमवेध्ये तु चित्रपुष्करसंज्ञके ॥
एवं वेध्यगणं कृत्वा दक्षिणेनेतरेण च ॥ 17 ॥
आरोहेत्प्रथमं धीरो जितलक्ष्यस्ततो नरः ॥
एष एव विधिः प्रोक्तस्तत्र दृष्टः प्रयोक्तृभिः ॥ 18 ॥

2.36.d:
आदिकं भ्रमणं तस्य तस्माद्विद्वन्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
लक्ष्यं संयोजयेत्तत्र प्रतियन्त्रगतं दृढम् ॥ 19 ॥
भ्रान्तं प्रचलितं चैव स्थितं यच्च भवेदिति ॥
समन्ताच्छादयेत्पश्चाच्छेदयेच्छ्लथयेदपि ॥ 2.180.20 ॥
कर्मयोगविधानज्ञो ज्ञात्वैवं विधिमाचरेत् ॥
मनसा चक्षुषा दृष्ट्या योगं शिक्षन्न्यसंजयेत् ॥ 21 ॥
दत्त्वा प्रयुक्तं सुकृतं प्रमाणान्न्यसेत्समन्तात्पुटकान्विचित्रान् ॥
अप्यङ्गुलीयप्रतिमां जपेच्च वालङ्गताः काष्ठगतं प्रलम्बम् ॥ 22 ॥
सिद्धार्थकान्गुञ्जयवांश्च तस्मिन्न्यसेद्विधिज्ञो भ्रमरीरिकाञ्च ॥
मृत्पिण्डसंस्थान्फलकांक्षितांश्च कबन्धनिष्पावकपेलवाश्च ॥ 23 ॥
हंसान्मयूरान्कुररांस्तथा च कारण्डवांश्चैव शिलीमुखांश्च ॥
गृध्रानुलूकानथ वापि चाषान्कपोतगोधाशुकसारिकाश्च ॥ 24 ॥
2.36.m:
its primary circular motion has therefore been proclaimed, O wise one.
There he should firmly fix the target mounted on a mechanical device,
which may be rotating, moving, or standing still.
He should completely cover it, and afterwards cut or loosen it.
Knowing the rules of the practice of action, he should act according to the rule in this way.
Practicing union with mind, eye, and sight, he should release [the arrow].
Having applied [arrows] well-fashioned to measure, he should set diverse targets all around;
he should strike even the likeness of a ring, or a hanging wooden [target] attached to hair.
In that [training], the one knowing the rule should place mustard seeds, guñjā seeds, and barley corns, and a spinning target,
and desired targets standing on clay lumps, and soft targets made of headless husked grains,
and geese, peacocks, ospreys, kāraṇḍava ducks, and bees,
vultures, owls, or blue jays, pigeons, monitor lizards, parrots, and sārikā birds;

2.36.d:
पलाशमूलोर्णवपूर्ण देहांश्चर्मावबद्धां मृदुचित्रगात्राम् ॥
वस्त्रयन्त्रैर्विविधैः सुयुक्तां काष्ठावसक्तैर्बहुभिः प्रकारैः ॥ 25 ॥
चलान्स्थिरांश्चाप्रगतांश्च विद्धान्न्यसेद्यथान्यायमथोर्ध्वसंस्थान् ॥
व्याघ्रान्मृगेन्द्रान्पृषतान्रुरूंश्च मृगान्सगोकर्णवराहवक्त्रान् ॥ 26 ॥
गोमायुमार्जारशशांस्तथान्यानृक्षान्मृगाश्चन्द्रमयेन्दुपूर्णान् ॥

tigers, lions, spotted deer, ruru deer, and deer with ears like cows and boar-faces,
jackals, cats, hares, and other bears, and deer filled with moonlight,
and other deer approaching near; the one knowing the procedure [should strike] them mounted on mechanical devices,
as well as others of many kinds that have appeared, their bodies bound in diverse postures.
Stationed in the rotation of arrows, he should strike them threefold with diverse combinations of aim.

striking against, roaring, piercing, and terrifying and brandishing: / know [these] actions of the pike, the sixth being designated 'sniffing'.
Striking the eyes, striking the arms, and striking the flanks, O Bhārgava, / straight, crooked, and thrusting: [these] are proclaimed [the actions] of the lance.
Joined, extended, leftward, zigzag like cow-urine, moving like a lotus, / then bent half-way, left and right,
turned around, turned back, kicked up by the feet, unobstructed, / and the swan's path and wrong path: [these] are proclaimed the actions of the mace.
The terrifying, monastery-felling, the ten calamities, / thrown, held in hand, and empty: one should designate [these] of the battle-axe.
Beating, cutting, O Rāma, and crushing: / these are the actions of the mallet, and also of the club.
Edge, middle, turned back, and half-command: / these indeed are the actions of the thunderbolt, and likewise of the paṭṭiśa.

2.183
॥ पुष्कर उवाच ॥
सन्नद्धैश्चर्मिभिर्भाव्यं तथा बद्धकृपाणिभिः ॥
चर्माणि तत्र वैयाघ्रमाहिषाण्यृषभाणि च ॥ 1 ॥
खेटकाद्यथ वा राम चर्माणि प्रभवन्ति तु ॥
तथा वरणमुख्यानि खड्गानि विविधानि च ॥ 2 ॥
बद्धादिभिः सतूणीरैस्तथा राम सतोमरैः ॥
बद्धगोधाङ्गुलित्राणैर्बद्धादर्शैर्विभीषणैः ॥ 3 ॥
तथा परश्वधोपेतै राम स्वासनयोधिभिः ॥ 4 ॥
गदाधरास्तथैवात्र सकृत्पाणिपरिच्छदाः ॥
सुसंनद्धा सुमनसो भवेयुर्विपुलौजसः ॥ 5 ॥
यत्र यस्य विशेषेण शस्त्रास्त्रैर्वातकौशलम् ॥
तदेव तस्य निर्दिष्टं यथावन्मनुजोत्तम ॥ 6 ॥
2.37.m:
The principal actions have been told to you regarding the chief weapons, O hero among men; / these are the names and forms to be known, each according to its nature.
Puṣkara said: / [The warriors] must be armored, bearing shields, and with girded daggers. / The shields there should be of tiger, buffalo, and bull hides,
or shields made of bucklers and so forth, O Rāma; / likewise, the foremost shields and various types of swords,
with bound [weapons] and the like, with quivers, and, O Rāma, with lances; / with fastened arm-guards and finger-guards, with fastened breastplates, formidable,
and equipped with battle-axes, O Rāma, fighters proficient with the bow.
Likewise, mace-bearers here, accompanied by attendants with daggers, / well-armored, resolute-minded, should possess vast energy.
Wherever and in whatever skill one is especially proficient with weapons or missiles, / precisely that is prescribed for him, properly, O best of men.

2.37.d:
सखलीनाः सपर्याणास्तथा सास्तरणा हयाः ॥
कार्याः सकवचा युद्धे चामरापीडधारिणः ॥ 7 ॥
अश्वी भवेत्सुसन्नद्धो रश्मिप्रग्रहकोविदः ॥
तथा सावरणो राम सकृपाणी परिच्छदः ॥ 8 ॥
बद्धासिर्बद्धजीवश्च तुरगारूढपिण्डकः ॥
ससुप्रासो भवेद्राम नानायुधधरस्तथा ॥ 9 ॥
रथः कार्यस्तथा युक्तः ईषादण्डकबन्धुरैः ॥
सुचक्रोपस्करयुतः सर्वरूपः पताकराट् ॥ 2.183.10 ॥
त्रिवेणुसंततश्चैव वैयाघ्रपरिवारणः ॥
किंकिणीजालनिर्घोषस्तथा वै सुप्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 11 ॥
उपासङ्गैर्निषङ्गैश्च तूणीरैर्वरकार्मुकैः ॥
सर्वायुधैरुपेतश्च तथा वृक्षादनीयुतः ॥12॥
तोयजीरकपिण्डीभिर्युक्तः शृङ्गैस्तथैव च ॥
सन्नद्धः सारथिस्तत्र भवेद्राम प्रतोदवान् ॥ 13 ॥
रश्मिग्रहणविच्चापि तथा मण्डलकोविदः ॥
तथाश्वहृदयज्ञश्च दूरदृष्टिः सुयन्त्रितः ॥ 14 ॥
2.37.m:
With bits, with saddles, and with saddlecloths, the horses / should be equipped with armor in battle, wearing chowries and crests.
The cavalryman should be well-armored, skilled in holding the reins, / and with a shield, O Rāma, having a dagger and equipment,
with fastened sword, fastened bowstring, firm in riding a horse, / with a good spear, O Rāma, and bearing various weapons.
The chariot should likewise be prepared, fitted with lovely yoke-poles and shafts, / equipped with good wheels and accessories, of all forms, splendid with banners,
covered with three woven bands, shielded with tiger skin, / having the sound of nets of jingling bells, and indeed very stable;
with quivers, arrow-cases, quivers, excellent bows, / equipped with all weapons, and furnished with missile-throwers,
furnished with water, cumin, flour balls, and likewise with horns; / armored there, O Rāma, the charioteer should have a goad,
knowing how to take the reins, and skilled in circular movements, / and knowing the horse's nature, far-sighted, well-controlled,

2.37.d:
स्वासनः कालविच्चैव बद्धासिः पाशसंयुतः ॥
पार्ष्णिः स्यादायुधज्ञस्य तथैवायुधकोविदः ॥ 15 ॥
चिरेण मूले यस्य स्यादवस्थानं महाभुजः ॥
पताकावरणं यस्य आयुधानां समर्पणम् ॥ 16 ॥
समायान्तं महाभागं तथा सारथिरक्षणम ॥
स्यातां धनुर्धरौ तत्र तथा च रथिनावुभौ ॥ 17 ॥
योधौ धनुर्भृतां श्रेष्ठ सर्वायुधविशारदौ ॥
तुरगाश्च सुसंनद्धा दान्ताः कार्यास्तथा रथे ॥ ॥ 18 ॥
तुल्यवेगबलाश्चैव तथा लघुपरिच्छदाः ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि तव नागेन्द्रकल्पनम् ॥ 19 ॥
कुञ्जरः स्यात्सुसन्नद्धः सपर्याणः कुथा वृतः ॥
सर्वायुधधरश्चैव तथा योधा वरायुधाः ॥2.183.20 ॥
परश्वधकराश्चैव तोयजीरकसंयुताः ॥
सम्यग्विभाज्याश्च तथा शृङ्खलावततास्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
2.37.m:
sitting well, knowing time, with fastened sword, provided with a noose; / the rear-guard should know weapons, likewise being skilled in arms,
whose long-established place is at the base, mighty-armed, / who shields the banner and supplies weapons,
and protects the charioteer when an illustrious [foe] approaches. / There should be two archers there, and both should be car-warriors,
two warriors, O best of bowmen, skilled in all weapons. / The horses on the chariot should be well-armored and trained,
of equal speed and strength, and lightly equipped. / Hereafter I shall declare to you the preparation of royal elephants.
The elephant should be well-armored, with a saddle, covered with a carpet, / carrying all weapons, and the warriors [upon it] bearing excellent weapons.
[They should be] holding battle-axes in hand, provided with water and cumin, / properly stationed, and likewise equipped with chains.

2.37.d:
पताका च तथा कार्या कुञ्जरस्य सुशोभना ॥
वराङ्कुशधरौ तत्र स्यातां मनुजपुङ्गवौ ॥ 22 ॥
एकः पृष्ठस्थितस्तत्र द्वितीयः स्कन्धगो भवेत् ॥
योधौ द्वौ वरधानुष्कौ द्वौ च खड्गधरौ दरौ ॥ 23 ॥
तयोरनुभवेतां वै तथा रक्षापरायणौ ॥
एकः पार्ष्णिस्थितस्तत्र वरशक्तिपताकधृक् ॥ 24 ॥
पालयेज्जघनं यद्वत्कुञ्जरस्य महामते ॥
एवं परस्परायत्ता रक्षा तेषां यथा भवेत् ॥ 25 ॥
महामात्रस्य धर्मज्ञ तथा च गजयोधिनः ॥
एवमेव तथा रक्ष्यो रथिनः स रथी भवेत् ॥ 26 ॥
कुञ्जरस्य तु रक्षार्थं भवेद्रथचतुष्टयम् ॥
रथेरथे गजे वापि तुरगाणां त्रयं भवेत् ॥ 27 ॥
धानुष्काणां त्रयं प्रोक्तं रक्षार्थं तुरगस्य च ॥
धन्विनो रक्षणार्थाय वर्मिणोऽपि नियोजयेत् ॥ 28 ॥
2.37.m:
And a very splendid banner should be fixed upon the elephant. / Two bull-like men should be there, wielding excellent goads:
one of them stationed on the back, and the second should be on the neck. / Two warriors should be excellent bowmen, and two holding swords [...],
and devoted to protecting them both. / Stationed at the rear should be one bearing an excellent spear and banner,
so that he protects the hindquarters of the elephant, O wise one. / In this way their mutual protection should be arranged,
of the elephant-driver, O knower of dharma, and of the elephant-warrior. / In this very same way, a chariot-warrior must be protected by another chariot-warrior.
For the protection of an elephant, there should be four chariots. / For every chariot or elephant, there should be three horses.
Three bowmen are prescribed for the protection of a horse; / for the protection of an archer, one should also deploy armored soldiers.

2.37.s:
kāryaṃ sarvaṃ susaṃbādhaṃ tathā toraṇarakṣaṇam ..
yojanā ca tathā kāryā yathā tu syāddhṛtikramaḥ .. 29 ..
2.37.d:
कार्यं सर्वं सुसंबाधं तथा तोरणरक्षणम् ॥
योजना च तथा कार्या यथा तु स्याद्धृतिक्रमः ॥ 29 ॥
2.37.m: All defense must be made impenetrable, as also the protection of gates; / and deployment should be made in such a way that there is orderly steadfastness,

2.37.s: saṃbādhaśca tathā rāma na bhavecca parasparam .. 2.183.30 ..
2.37.d: संबाधश्च तथा राम न भवेच्च परस्परम् ॥ 2.183.30 ॥
2.37.m: and also so that mutual congestion does not occur, O Rāma.

2.37.s:
nāgendrakalpaṃ tava sarvayuktaṃ saṃkṣepato bhārgavavaṃśa mukhya..
etattu kṛtvāpi naraḥ sayuddhe jayatyavaśyaṃ samupārjane ca .. 31 ..
2.37.d:
नागेन्द्रकल्पं तव सर्वयुक्तं संक्षेपतो भार्गववंश मुख्य॥
एतत्तु कृत्वापि नरः सयुद्धे जयत्यवश्यं समुपार्जने च ॥ 31 ॥
2.37.m: The entire preparation of lordly elephants has been related to you in brief, O foremost of the Bhrgu lineage! / Having done this, a man is surely victorious in battle and in acquisition.

2.37.s:
iti śrīviṣṇumahāpurāṇe dvitīyabhāge śrīviṣṇudharmottare dvitīyakhaṇḍe mārkaṇḍeyavajrasaṃvāde rāmaṃ prati puṣkaropākhyāne dhanurvede vāhanasajjīkaraṇo nāma tryaśītyuttaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 183 .. ..
samāpto'yaṃ viṣṇudharmottaradvitīyakhaṇḍaḥ .
2.37.d:
इति श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे द्वितीयभागे श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे द्वितीयखण्डे मार्कण्डेयवज्रसंवादे रामं प्रति पुष्करोपाख्याने धनुर्वेदे वाहनसज्जीकरणो नाम त्र्यशीत्युत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ 183 ॥ ॥
समाप्तोऽयं विष्णुधर्मोत्तरद्वितीयखण्डः ।
2.37.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and eighty-third chapter, entitled 'Equipping the Mounts' in the Dhanurveda, within the discourse of Puṣkara to Rāma, in the conversation between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the second book of the venerable Viṣṇudharmottara, [part of] the second section in the venerable Viṣṇu Mahāpurāṇa.
Here ends the second book of the Viṣṇudharmottara.

2.38.m: Now the second book [table of contents]:
1. Rāma’s arrival at Puṣkara's house.
2. Praise of the king in the realm.
3. Characteristics of a king.
4. Characteristics of an astrologer.
5. Characteristics of the royal priest.
6. Characteristics of royal ministers.
7. Characteristics of the chief queen of a king.
8. Characteristics of an eminent man.
9. Characteristics of an eminent woman.
10. Characteristics of auspicious elephants.
11. Auspicious and inauspicious marks of horses.
12. Characteristics of the fly-whisk.
13. Characteristics of the parasol.
14. Characteristics of the royal throne.

2.38.s: 158 āśvinaśuklanavamyāṃ śivirottare bhadrakālīgṛhaṃ nirmāya paṭe bhadrakālīṃ sampūjyāṣṭamyāṃ chatravarmādyāyudhāni pūjayet
2.38.d: 158 आश्विनशुक्लनवम्यां शिविरोत्तरे भद्रकालीगृहं निर्माय पटे भद्रकालीं सम्पूज्याष्टम्यां छत्रवर्माद्यायुधानि पूजयेत्

163. The rule of omens on a journey.
164. The rule of omens on a journey.
165. The outcome of inquiries regarding auspicious and inauspicious signs.
[Chapter] 166. Description of the branches of the science in the exposition of astronomy.

[Chapter] 167. Exposition of the measures of time, zodiacal signs, planetary natures, the seven divisions, planetary friendships, and the limbs of the embryo month by month; and exposition of the nourishment of the embryo and so forth through the strength of the lord of the month, the determination of planetary life-spans, the causes of death, the aṣṭavarga, royal yogas, and so on.

Description of solar and other days, the measures of the Kṛta and other ages, the aeon, planetary revolutions, planetary orbits, the calculation of sines and so on, the calculation of declination and celestial latitude, the derivation of the measure of the ascendant, the polar longitudes of the lunar mansions, the retrogradation and other motions of Mars and other [planets], the cardinal points, and so on.

[Chapter] 171. Knowledge of the elapsed and remaining parts of the day by means of the divisor, the gnomon's shadow, and so forth.

[Chapter] 174. Calculation of the gnomon, the base of the gnomon, the base-sine, parallax in longitude, parallax in latitude, the true celestial latitude, immersion, emersion, and so forth of the sun and moon at the time of an eclipse, and description of the excellence of knowing planetary motion.
