2.38.m: [Chapter] 175. Fixed and mobile planets; the excellence of a king's march when the mobile planets are strong; its prohibition at the setting of Venus and so forth; followed by an exposition of the months, days, lunar mansions, directional gate-mansions, ascendants, lunar days, and yogas of success suitable for a march; and the granting of success in a march in the upacaya mansions of one's birth-sign and so forth.

2.38.s: 176 rājñāṃ vijayayātrāyai śubhanakṣatraṃ vicārya taddinātsaptarātrapūrvavidheyavidhivarṇanapurassaraṃ yātrādivase trivikramaṃ sampūjya homānantaraṃ yātrika sūktādipaṭhanapūrvakaṃ diṅnakṣatrayornaivedyaṃ dattvā kiñcitprāśya yāyāt
2.38.d: 176 राज्ञां विजययात्रायै शुभनक्षत्रं विचार्य तद्दिनात्सप्तरात्रपूर्वविधेयविधिवर्णनपुरस्सरं यात्रादिवसे त्रिविक्रमं सम्पूज्य होमानन्तरं यात्रिक सूक्तादिपठनपूर्वकं दिङ्नक्षत्रयोर्नैवेद्यं दत्त्वा किञ्चित्प्राश्य यायात्
2.38.m: [Chapter] 176. Having determined an auspicious lunar mansion for the victorious march of kings, preceded by a description of the rites to be performed for seven nights prior to that day, one should worship Trivikrama on the day of the march, and after the fire sacrifice, preceded by the recitation of the hymn for marching and so on, having offered food to the direction and the lunar mansion and eaten a little, one should set out.
[Chapter] 177. Description of battle, preceded by the donning of armour, weapons, and so on, and the deployment of infantry, cavalry, chariots, elephants, and so forth.

[Chapter] 178. The four divisions of archery based on the feet of chariots, elephants, horses, and infantry; battle conducted through the possession of arms and missiles that are machine-released, hand-released, released-and-held, and unreleased.
[Chapter] 179. Description of archery postures: samapada, vaiśākha, maṇḍala, ālīḍha, pratyālīḍha, sampuṭa, and so forth.
[Chapter] 180. Description of training and practice in manual dexterity and so on in the operation of arrows.
[Chapter] 181. Description of the threefold arrow method in archery.
[Chapter] 182. Combat actions with the sword, javelin, trident, iron club, mace, battle-axe, mallet, club, thunderbolt, broad-bladed spear, knife, sling, and mace.

[Chapter] 183. Description of horses equipped with bits, saddles, blankets, and so on, of charioteers skilled in controlling the reins and equipped with armour, and of chariots, elephants, and the like.
Thus ends the Second Book of the Viṣṇudharmottara.

3.0.s:
oṃ śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ..
.. oṃnamo nārāyaṇāya ..
.. atha śrīviṣṇumahāpurāṇe viṣṇudharmottaratṛtīyakhaṇḍaprārambhaḥ ..
3.0.d:
ओं श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
॥ ओंनमो नारायणाय ॥
॥ अथ श्रीविष्णुमहापुराणे विष्णुधर्मोत्तरतृतीयखण्डप्रारम्भः ॥
3.0.m:
Oṃ, homage to the blessed Gaṇeśa.
Oṃ, homage to Nārāyaṇa.
Now begins the Third Book of the Viṣṇudharmottara in the illustrious Viṣṇu Mahāpurāṇa.

3.1.s:
.. vajra uvāca ..
kiṃ kartavyaṃ manuṣyeṇa kiṃ kurvansukhamedhate ..
asmim̐lloke pare caiva kenāpnoti mahatsukham .. 1 ..
3.1.d:
॥ वज्र उवाच ॥
किं कर्तव्यं मनुष्येण किं कुर्वन्सुखमेधते ॥
अस्मिम्̐ल्लोके परे चैव केनाप्नोति महत्सुखम् ॥ 1 ॥
3.1.m:
Vajra said:
What should be done by a human being? Doing what does one prosper in happiness? / How does one attain great happiness in this world and in the next? (1)

3.1.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca .. ..
antarvedi bahirvedi puruṣeṇa vijānatā ..
devatāpūjanaṃ kāryaṃ lokadvayamabhīpsatā .. 2 ..
3.1.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
अन्तर्वेदि बहिर्वेदि पुरुषेण विजानता ॥
देवतापूजनं कार्यं लोकद्वयमभीप्सता ॥ 2 ॥
3.1.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Desiring both worlds, a discerning man should worship the gods / both inside the sacrificial enclosure and outside the sacrificial enclosure. (2)

3.1.s:
yajñeṣu devayajanamantarvedi prakīrtitam ..
bahirvedi tathaivoktamupavāsavratādikam ..
iṣṭāpūrtena labhyante ye lokāstānbubhūṣatā .. 3 ..
3.1.d:
यज्ञेषु देवयजनमन्तर्वेदि प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
बहिर्वेदि तथैवोक्तमुपवासव्रतादिकम् ॥
इष्टापूर्तेन लभ्यन्ते ये लोकास्तान्बुभूषता ॥ 3 ॥
3.1.m: Sacrificing to the gods in Vedic rites is declared to be inside the enclosure; / fasts, vows, and the like are likewise stated to be outside the enclosure. / One wishing to attain those worlds which are gained through sacrificial and charitable works (3)

3.1.s:
devānāmālayaḥ kāryo dvayamapyatra dṛśyate ..
viśeṣeṇa kalau kāle kartavyaṃ devatāgṛham .. 4 ..
3.1.d:
देवानामालयः कार्यो द्वयमप्यत्र दृश्यते ॥
विशेषेण कलौ काले कर्तव्यं देवतागृहम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.1.m: should make an abode for the gods; both [forms of merit] are seen in this. / Especially in the Kali age, a temple for the gods should be made. (4)

3.1.s:
kṛtatretādvāpareṣu narāḥ paśyanti devatām ..
tiṣyaṃ prāpya na paśyanti pūjāstvarcāgatā yataḥ .. 5 ..
3.1.d:
कृतत्रेताद्वापरेषु नराः पश्यन्ति देवताम् ॥
तिष्यं प्राप्य न पश्यन्ति पूजास्त्वर्चागता यतः ॥ 5 ॥
3.1.m: In the Kṛta, Tretā, and Dvāpara ages, men behold the deity; / having reached the Kali age, they do not behold [the deity], because worship is directed to images. (5)

3.1.s:
kṛtādiṣvapi dṛṣṭvā ca devānmanujasattama ..
arcāgataviśeṣeṇa pūjayanti vidhānataḥ .. 6 ..
3.1.d:
कृतादिष्वपि दृष्ट्वा च देवान्मनुजसत्तम ॥
अर्चागतविशेषेण पूजयन्ति विधानतः ॥ 6 ॥
3.1.m: Even in the Kṛta and other ages, O best of men, having beheld the gods, / they worship them according to rule, particularly when present in images. (6)

3.1.s:
citrasūtravidhānena devatārcāṃ vinirmitām ..
surūpāṃ pūjayedvidvāṃstatra saṃnihitā bhavet .. 7..
3.1.d:
चित्रसूत्रविधानेन देवतार्चां विनिर्मिताम् ॥
सुरूपां पूजयेद्विद्वांस्तत्र संनिहिता भवेत् ॥ 7॥
3.1.m: A wise man should worship an image of a deity fashioned / according to the rules of the Citrasūtra and well-proportioned; [the deity] will be present there. (7)

3.1.s:
svākārāṃ lakṣaṇopetāṃ yastāṃ saṃpūjayennaraḥ ..
sa sarvakāmānāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
asmim̐lloke pare caiva sukhavānsa bhavetsadā .. 8 ..
3.1.d:
स्वाकारां लक्षणोपेतां यस्तां संपूजयेन्नरः ॥
स सर्वकामानाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
अस्मिम्̐ल्लोके परे चैव सुखवान्स भवेत्सदा ॥ 8 ॥
3.1.m: A man who worships it properly shaped and endowed with the required characteristics / attains all desires; there is no doubt in this; / he will always be happy in this world and in the next. (8)

3.1.s:
athārcāṃ lakṣaṇairhīnāṃ yastu pūjayate naraḥ ..
tasyānarthā vivardhante tasmāttāṃ ca vivarjayet .. 9 ..
3.1.d:
अथार्चां लक्षणैर्हीनां यस्तु पूजयते नरः ॥
तस्यानर्था विवर्धन्ते तस्मात्तां च विवर्जयेत् ॥ 9 ॥
3.1.m: Now, as for the man who worships an image devoid of the required characteristics, / his misfortunes multiply; therefore, one should avoid it. (9)

3.1.s:
prāsādakaraṇaṃ puṇyaṃ devārcākaraṇaṃ tathā ..
surārcāpūjanaṃ puṇyaṃ tatra puṇyā namaskriyā .. 3.1.10 ..
3.1.d:
प्रासादकरणं पुण्यं देवार्चाकरणं तथा ॥
सुरार्चापूजनं पुण्यं तत्र पुण्या नमस्क्रिया ॥ 3.1.10 ॥
3.1.m: Building a temple is meritorious, as is making an image of a deity; / worship of a divine image is meritorious, and bowing down to it is meritorious. (10)

3.1.s:
tasmātsarvapratnena surārcāṃ lakṣaṇānvitām ..
kārayetpūjanaṃ vidvānna tvalakṣaṇasaṃyutām ..11 ..
3.1.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रत्नेन सुरार्चां लक्षणान्विताम् ॥
कारयेत्पूजनं विद्वान्न त्वलक्षणसंयुताम् ॥11 ॥
3.1.m: Therefore, with every effort a wise man should have an image of a deity made / endowed with the required characteristics, and worship it, never one devoid of characteristics. (11)

3.1.s:
dharmamarthaṃ tathā kāmaṃ mokṣaṃ ca yadunandana ..
prayacchanti mahārāja narāṇāmiha devatāḥ .. 12 ..
3.1.d:
धर्ममर्थं तथा कामं मोक्षं च यदुनन्दन ॥
प्रयच्छन्ति महाराज नराणामिह देवताः ॥ 12 ॥
3.1.m: Dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, O delight of the Yadus, / the gods bestow upon men here, O great king. (12)

3.1.s:
kāmāniṣṭānprayacchanti svargamatyantameva ca ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena nṛṇāṃ pūjyā divaukasaḥ .. 13 ..
3.1.d:
कामानिष्टान्प्रयच्छन्ति स्वर्गमत्यन्तमेव च ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन नृणां पूज्या दिवौकसः ॥ 13 ॥
3.1.m: They bestow cherished desires, and heaven that is supreme. / Therefore, with all effort the denizens of heaven must be worshipped by men. (13)

3.1.s:
nityaṃ narāṇāṃ surapūjakānāṃ lokā manojñāḥ sulabhā bhavanti ..
loke tathāsmindhanadhānyayuktāḥ samṛddhibhājaśca narā bhavanti .. 14 ..
3.2
vajra uvāca ..
devatārūpanirmāṇaṃ kathayasva mamānagha ..
yasmātsannihitā nityaṃ śāstravatsākṛtirbhavet..1..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
citrasūtraṃ na jānāti yastu samyaṅ narādhipa ..
pratimālakṣaṇaṃ vettuṃ na śakyantena karhicit .. 2 ..
vajra uvāca ..
citrasūtraṃ samācakṣva bhṛguvaṃśa vivardhana ..
citrasūtravidevātha vetti vāglakṣaṇaṃ yataḥ ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
vinā tu nṛtyaśāstreṇa citrasūtraṃ sudurvidam..3..
jagato na kriyā kāryā dvayorapi yato nṛpa ..
vajra uvāca ..
nṛtyaśāstraṃ samācakṣva citrasūtraṃ vadiṣyasi..
nṛtyaśāstravidhānaṃ ca citraṃ vetti yato dvija..4..
3.1.d:
नित्यं नराणां सुरपूजकानां लोका मनोज्ञाः सुलभा भवन्ति ॥
लोके तथास्मिन्धनधान्ययुक्ताः समृद्धिभाजश्च नरा भवन्ति ॥ 14 ॥
3.2
वज्र उवाच ॥
देवतारूपनिर्माणं कथयस्व ममानघ ॥
यस्मात्सन्निहिता नित्यं शास्त्रवत्साकृतिर्भवेत्॥1॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
चित्रसूत्रं न जानाति यस्तु सम्यङ् नराधिप ॥
प्रतिमालक्षणं वेत्तुं न शक्यन्तेन कर्हिचित् ॥ 2 ॥
वज्र उवाच ॥
चित्रसूत्रं समाचक्ष्व भृगुवंश विवर्धन ॥
चित्रसूत्रविदेवाथ वेत्ति वाग्लक्षणं यतः ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
विना तु नृत्यशास्त्रेण चित्रसूत्रं सुदुर्विदम्॥3॥
जगतो न क्रिया कार्या द्वयोरपि यतो नृप ॥
वज्र उवाच ॥
नृत्यशास्त्रं समाचक्ष्व चित्रसूत्रं वदिष्यसि॥
नृत्यशास्त्रविधानं च चित्रं वेत्ति यतो द्विज॥4॥
3.1.m:
For men who continually worship the gods, delightful worlds are easily obtained; / likewise in this world, men become endowed with wealth and grain, and enjoy prosperity. (14)
3.2
Vajra said:
Tell me, O sinless one, about the fashioning of the forms of the deities, / by which [an image] made according to the treatise may always possess their presence. (1)
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
He who does not thoroughly know the Citrasūtra, O lord of men, / can never know the characteristics of an image. (2)
Vajra said:
Explain the Citrasūtra, O promoter of the race of Bhṛgu, / since only he who knows the Citrasūtra knows the characteristics of sacred words.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Without the treatise on dance, the Citrasūtra is very hard to know; (3)
for no depiction of the world can be made by either of the two [without the other], O king.
Vajra said:
Explain the treatise on dance; you will [then] speak of the Citrasūtra, / since one who knows the rules of the treatise on dance knows painting, O twice-born one. (4)

3.1.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca..
ātodyaṃ yo na jānāti tasya vṛttaṃ hi durvidam ..
ātodyena vinā nṛttaṃ vidyate na kathaṃcana .. 5 ..
vajra uvāca ..
ātodyaṃ tvaṃ hi dharmajña nṛtyaśāstraṃ vadiṣyasi ..
tasminsuvidite vetti nṛtyaṃ bhārgavasattama..6..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
na gītena vinā śakyaṃ jñātumātodyamapyuta ..
gītaśāstravidhānajñaḥ sarvaṃ vetti yathāvidhi .. 7 ..
vajra uvāca ..
gītaśāstraṃ samācakṣva sarvadharmabhṛtāṃ vara ..
gītaśāstravidevātha sarvajñaḥ puruṣottamaḥ ..8 ..
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
saṃskṛtaṃ prākṛtaṃ caiva gītaṃ dvividhamucyate ..
apabhraṣṭaṃ tṛtīyaṃ ca tadanantaṃ narādhipa .. 9 ..
deśabhāṣāviśeṣeṇa tasyānto neha vidyate ..
gītaṃ pāṭhavaśājjñeyaṃ sa ca pāṭho dvidhā mataḥ..3.2.10..
gadyaṃ padyaṃ ca dharmajña gadyaṃ sakathayā smṛtam ..
padyaṃ chandoviśeṣeṇa cchandaśca bahudhā bhavet ..11 ..
3.1.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच॥
आतोद्यं यो न जानाति तस्य वृत्तं हि दुर्विदम् ॥
आतोद्येन विना नृत्तं विद्यते न कथंचन ॥ 5 ॥
वज्र उवाच ॥
आतोद्यं त्वं हि धर्मज्ञ नृत्यशास्त्रं वदिष्यसि ॥
तस्मिन्सुविदिते वेत्ति नृत्यं भार्गवसत्तम॥6॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
न गीतेन विना शक्यं ज्ञातुमातोद्यमप्युत ॥
गीतशास्त्रविधानज्ञः सर्वं वेत्ति यथाविधि ॥ 7 ॥
वज्र उवाच ॥
गीतशास्त्रं समाचक्ष्व सर्वधर्मभृतां वर ॥
गीतशास्त्रविदेवाथ सर्वज्ञः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥8 ॥
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
संस्कृतं प्राकृतं चैव गीतं द्विविधमुच्यते ॥
अपभ्रष्टं तृतीयं च तदनन्तं नराधिप ॥ 9 ॥
देशभाषाविशेषेण तस्यान्तो नेह विद्यते ॥
गीतं पाठवशाज्ज्ञेयं स च पाठो द्विधा मतः॥3.2.10॥
गद्यं पद्यं च धर्मज्ञ गद्यं सकथया स्मृतम् ॥
पद्यं छन्दोविशेषेण च्छन्दश्च बहुधा भवेत् ॥11 ॥
3.1.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
He who does not know instrumental music finds dance hard to know; / without instrumental music, dance cannot exist in any way. (5)
Vajra said:
You, O knower of dharma, will speak of instrumental music and the treatise on dance; / when that is well known, one understands dance, O best of the Bhṛgus. (6)
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Even instrumental music cannot be understood without vocal music;
he who knows the rules of the science of vocal music knows everything according to rule.
Vajra said:
Explain the science of vocal music, O best of all maintainers of dharma;
indeed, one who knows the science of vocal music is all-knowing, the highest of men.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Vocal music is said to be of two kinds: Sanskrit and Prakrit;
and the third is Apabhraṃśa, which is endless, O lord of men.
Through the distinctions of regional languages, there is no end to it here;
vocal music is to be known through recitation, and that recitation is considered twofold:
prose and verse, O knower of dharma. Prose is held [to be used] in narrative;
verse is [defined] by specific metres, and metre can be of many kinds.

3.1.s:
gadyapadyānubhāvena jñeyau lakṣaṇasaṃyutau ..
padyaṃ ca dvividhaṃ tatra suvṛtramatimuktakam.. 12 ..
ekaviṃśatisaṃkhyāḥ syuḥ supaḥ suptiṅparaṃ smṛtam ..
prathamaḥ puruṣastveko dvitīyo madhyamo mataḥ .. 13 ..
uttamākhyastṛtīyastu tatkriyāvacanaṃ trikam ..
tiṅaśca navakaṃ tatra parasmaipadasaṃjñakam .. .. 14 ..
3.1.d:
गद्यपद्यानुभावेन ज्ञेयौ लक्षणसंयुतौ ॥
पद्यं च द्विविधं तत्र सुवृत्रमतिमुक्तकम्॥ 12 ॥
एकविंशतिसंख्याः स्युः सुपः सुप्तिङ्परं स्मृतम् ॥
प्रथमः पुरुषस्त्वेको द्वितीयो मध्यमो मतः ॥ 13 ॥
उत्तमाख्यस्तृतीयस्तु तत्क्रियावचनं त्रिकम् ॥
तिङश्च नवकं तत्र परस्मैपदसंज्ञकम् ॥ ॥ 14 ॥

3.1.s:
ātmanepadasaṃjñaṃ ca navakaṃ parikīrtitam ..
yuṣmadyupapade tatra madhyamaḥ puruṣo bhavet .. 15 ..
3.1.d:
आत्मनेपदसंज्ञं च नवकं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
युष्मद्युपपदे तत्र मध्यमः पुरुषो भवेत् ॥ 15 ॥

and nine are taught under the name of middle voice.

विंशतिस्त्वेकसंयुक्ता प्रकृतिः परिकीर्तिता॥
द्वाविंशतिश्च कथितं तथैवाकृतिसंज्ञकम ॥7॥
त्रयोविंशतिश्च विकृतिः सा चैकात्संकृतिर्मता ॥
संकृतिश्चैकसंयुक्ता कथिता विकृतिर्नृप ॥8॥
षड्विंशतिश्चातिकृतिश्छन्दश्चोक्तं मनीषिभिः ॥
यथायथं चतुर्भिः स्वैः पादैरेतानि निर्दिशेत् ॥ 9 ॥
मात्रकस्तु लघुर्वर्णः स्पष्टलेखाभिचिह्नितः ॥
संस्थाप्यः स्याद्द्विमात्रस्तु गुरुर्वक्रस्तथा भवेत् ॥ 3.3.10 ॥
लघुश्चान्त्यश्च यो वर्णः स गुरुश्च भवेन्नृप ॥
दीर्घप्लुतौ च कथितौ तथैव गुरुसंज्ञकौ ॥11 ॥
संयोगाद्याः परे यस्मात्स लघुश्च गुरुः स्मृतः ॥
लघुगुरुविभागेन प्रस्तारोनेन यादव ॥ 12 ॥
सर्वे छन्दोविकल्पाश्च भवन्ति बहुशो नृप ॥

3.1.d:
यावत्संख्याक्षरं च्छंदस्तावन्तो गुरुवो नृप ॥
स्थाप्या अधश्च पूर्वाणां लघु पूर्वस्य विन्यसेत् ॥ 14 ॥
अतोऽन्येषु त्ववस्थाप्यं नृपमुख्य यथास्थितम् ॥
एवमेव विधिं कुर्यादादिश्च गुरुभिः पुनः ॥ 15 ॥
पूरयेदक्षरैस्तावत्कुर्यादेतं नृपोत्तम ॥
यावदक्षरसंख्या स्युः सर्वे हि लघवो नृप ॥ 16 ॥
एतत्स्यादक्षरैच्छन्दो मात्राश्छन्दास्तथैव हि ॥
उक्तवर्णाक्षरं छन्दो भवेदेकविवर्जितः ॥ 17 ॥
यदा तदा निवृत्संज्ञो ह्यधिकेन तमत्तथा ॥
वर्णद्वयेन रहितं विराडिति हि शब्दितम् ॥ 18 ॥
अधिकं च सुरासंज्ञं कथितं यदुसत्तम ॥
तेभ्यो भवन्ति सर्वाणि मात्राच्छन्दांसि यादव ॥ 19 ॥
दिङ्मात्रमेतत्कथितं नरेन्द्र विस्तारजिज्ञासुरतो मनुष्यः ॥
संसाधयेत्तत्स्वधिया यथावत्सुदुस्तरं विस्तरशो हि वक्तुम् ॥ 3.3.20 ॥
3.1.m:
As many syllables as the metre has, so many heavy ones, O king,
are to be set down; and below the previous ones, one should place a light syllable of the former.
Then in the others, O foremost of kings, it should be placed as it stands;
one should perform this same procedure, and beginning again with heavy syllables,
one should fill it with syllables, doing this until, O best of kings,
all the syllables become light in number, O king.
This is metre by syllables, and likewise metre by morae.
A metre lacking one syllable from the stated syllables
is then called Nicṛt; and with an additional one, it is [called] Bhūrij.
That which is deprived of two syllables is named Virāj;
and that which has [two] additional is called Svarāj, O best of the Yadus.
From them arise all the moraic metres, O Yādava.
This has been told merely as an indication, O ruler of men; from this a man desiring to know the full extent
should accomplish it with his own intellect properly, for it is very difficult to explain in detail.

मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
तत्राज्ञायुक्तमद्वैधं दीप्तं गम्भीरशब्दवत् ॥
क्वचिन्निरुक्तसंयुक्तं वाक्यमेतत्स्वयंभुवः ॥ 1 ॥
यत्किंचिन्मिश्रसंयुक्तं युक्तं नाम विभक्तिभिः ॥
प्रत्यक्षाभिहितं यच्च तादृशीनां वचः स्मृतम् ॥ 2 ॥
नैगमैर्विविधैः शब्दैर्निपातं बहुलं च यत् ॥
न चापि सुमहद्वाक्यमृचीकानां वचः स्मृतम् ॥ 3 ॥
अविस्पष्टपदं ज्ञेयमृषिपुत्रवचो नृप ॥
भूतभव्यभवज्ञानं जन्मदुःखविकुत्सनम् ॥ 4 ॥
मित्राणां तद्भवेद्वाक्यं गर्भेषु च प्रवर्तनम् ॥
आज्ञायुक्तं च वचनं तथा हेतुविवर्जितम् ॥ 5 ॥
राजर्षीणां तु विज्ञेयं बह्वर्थं बहुविस्तरम् ॥
बह्वभिधानं बह्वर्थे देवतानां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 6 ॥
बह्वभिधानमल्पार्थं दानवानां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
अल्पाभिधानमल्पार्थं गन्धर्वाणां तथा भवेत् ॥ 7 ॥
3.1.m:
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
There, speech which is authoritative, unambiguous, brilliant, with deep sound,
and sometimes accompanied by etymology, is the speech of the Self-born [Brahmā].
Speech which is somewhat mixed, furnished with nominal case-endings,
and refers to what is directly perceived, is held to be the speech of women like that.
Speech which abounds in various Vedic words and particles,
and is not very long, is remembered as the speech of the Ṛcīkas.
The speech of sons of sages is to be known as having indistinct words, O king.
Knowledge of past, future, and present, and reviling of the misery of birth:
that is the speech of friends, as well as directing [the mind] to the origins [of things].
Speech that is commanding and devoid of reasoning
is to be known as that of royal seers, with much meaning and extensive elaboration.
Speech with many names for many meanings is proclaimed as that of the gods.
That which has many words and little meaning is proclaimed to belong to the dānavas. / That which has few words and little meaning belongs likewise to the gandharvas.

3.1.d:
दुर्बोधं विषमं चैव राक्षसानां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
गूढाक्षरं तु यक्षाणां किन्नरैरुक्तवत्तथा ॥ 8 ॥
नागानामतिविस्पष्टं पुनरुक्तसमन्वितम् ॥
रागद्वेषसमायुक्तं हेतुमत्पौरुषं भवेत् ॥9॥
मन्त्रा नवविधाः प्रोक्ताः ऋग्यजुःसामलक्षणाः ॥
स्तुतिर्निन्दा प्रशंसा च आक्रोशः प्रेष्य एव च ॥ 3.4.10 ॥
प्रश्नोऽनुज्ञा तथाख्यानमाशास्तिर्विषया मताः ॥
एवं ते सर्वविद्यानां विहितं सर्वलक्षणम् ॥॥॥
पौरुषे विद्यते तच्च नान्यत्रेति विनिश्चयः ॥
स्वभावान्न च्यवन्त्येव ये प्रोक्ता नरवर्जिंताः ॥ 12 ॥
दृश्यते हि पुमान्कश्चित्कश्चिच्छ्रेष्ठतमो धिया ॥
तस्मात्तत्रैव तस्योक्ता बुद्धिः श्रेष्ठतमा नृप ॥ 13 ॥
एतन्मयोक्तं सुपरीक्षणं ते वाक्यस्य भो वाक्यविदां वरिष्ठ ॥
विचक्षणैरत्र च रागतस्तु ज्ञेयं तथा द्वेषसमागमाच्च ॥ 14 ॥
3.1.m:
That which is difficult to comprehend and irregular is proclaimed to belong to the rākṣasas. / That which has hidden syllables belongs to the yakṣas, and similarly [speech] as spoken by the kinnaras.
That which is exceedingly clear and accompanied by repetitions belongs to the nāgas. / Human [speech] is accompanied by attachment and aversion, and is endowed with reasoning.
Mantras characterized by the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma [Vedas] are said to be of nine kinds: / praise, blame, commendation, abuse, and command,
question, permission, narration, and benediction are considered their topics. / Thus the full definition of all sciences has been laid down for you […] / And that is found in human [speech] and not elsewhere; this is the conclusion. / Those who are not human never depart from their own nature.
For a certain man is seen [to be ordinary], while a certain man is supreme in intellect; / therefore, O king, his intellect is said to be supreme precisely therein.
This excellent examination of speech has been spoken by me to you, O best of those who know speech; / and here it should be understood by the wise through attachment and through the presence of aversion.

3.1.m:
Whether it equals divine speech or speech of the ṛṣis, or whether it equals other speech, / the speech of men, O king, is to be understood as arising from attachment and from the presence of aversion.
3.5 / Having few syllables, free from ambiguity, containing the essence, facing in all directions, / free from superfluous words, and blameless: such is an aphorism known to those who know aphorisms.
It is proclaimed to be of two kinds: general rule and exception. / The aphorism, the counter-exclusion, the example, O king,
and the counter-example are proclaimed to be the four limbs. / And the sentence, the meaning of the sentence, the meaning of the word, and the word itself—
this too is proclaimed elsewhere as four limbs. / Thesis, reason, example, application,
and conclusion are accepted as the five members [of a syllogism]. / The initial statement, the connection, the meaning of the aphorism, its qualification,
the objection, and the resolution: this is the sixfold exposition of an aphorism. / For all that is cited [and] exemplified is indeed contained in aphorisms.

अपार्थं व्याहतं चैव पुनरुक्तं तथैव च ॥

आभासमनुमानस्य वाष्परेणुचयौ यथा ॥ 13 ॥
3.1.m:
What is spoken at great length destroys the intellect; what is spoken too concisely is not grasped. / Leaving aside conciseness and verbosity, one should state what one intends to say.
One should avoid that which is devoid of meaning, contradictory, tautological, / similarly of disjointed arrangement, and devoid of logic.
Breach of order, division [of an indivisible rule], an overly heavy aphorism, / and alteration of an expression: these should not occur without a reason.
Having made all the word-analysis, and immediately thereafter the compound analysis, / when the compound analysis has been made, the wise man should explain the meaning.
The meaning of the aphorism, the meaning of the words, the reason, the sequence, / the etymology, and the arrangement: this is the sixfold exposition of a rule.
Perception, inference, and authoritative testimony: / endowed with these three means of valid knowledge, a treatise is entitled to authoritativeness.
Pseudo-perception is also mentioned, such as a mirage; / an apparent inference is like a mass of vapor or dust,

which generates the doubt of smoke, but does not lead to the apprehension of fire. / But that which is uttered by an untrustworthy person who makes a show of trustworthiness,
that, O best of kings, they call pseudo-authoritative testimony. / One who is completely free from attachment and aversion is called authoritative.
Know etymological interpretation to be twofold: established and natural. / What is to be derived is established, but the establishment of the meaning is eternal.
Therein, all [terms] like 'cow', 'horse', and 'man' are natural. / It is declared to be of ten kinds by the tradition; I shall state that as it has been received:
the categorical, the causal, the manifested, the conventional, the artificial, / the metaphorical, the relational, the secondary, and the derivative.
We see the secondary from a quality, such as 'great' and the like; / and from a cause, the causal, as 'broken', 'shaven', and the like.
Metaphorically [one says] 'devoted' because of devotion, 'man-lion' because of the mouth, or 'mother-like' toward one who is not a mother. / And where they speak alike, that is convention, such as 'a courtesan'.
The artificial is that which is made, such as Devadatta and the like. / Metaphor arises from figurative transference, as 'oil-noose' or 'balance'.

अथ तन्त्रयुक्तयो भवन्ति अधिकरणं योगः पदार्थः हेत्वर्थ उद्देशो निदेशः प्रदेशोतिदेशः अपवर्गो वाक्यविशेषोर्थापत्तिः प्रसंग एकान्तो नैकान्तः पूर्वपक्षो निर्णयो विधानपर्यायोतिक्रान्तावेक्षणं संशयो व्याख्यानमनुमतिस्वसंज्ञानिर्वचनं दृष्टान्तो वियोगो विकल्पः समुच्चयोर्थ इति ।
तदधिकरणं येन वाक्यार्थो युज्यते संयोगो योर्थो विकृतसूत्रपदं स पदार्थो यदन्यत युक्तिमदर्थस्य साधनं स हेत्वर्थः ।
समासवचनमुद्देशो विस्तरवचनं निर्देश एवमेवेत्युपदेशोनेन कारणेनेत्यपदेशः ॥ प्रकृतस्यानागतेन साधनं प्रदेशोतिक्रामणेन सति देशोभिप्रायानुकर्षणमपवर्गो येनार्थः परिसमाप्यते ।
पदेनाहार्येण स वाक्यशेषो यदकीर्तितमर्यादामापद्यते सार्थापत्तिः । प्रकरणाभिहितोक्तः केनचिदुपोद्धातेन पुनरुद्दिश्यमानः प्रसंगः सर्वत्र यत्तथा स एकान्तः क्वचित्तथा क्वचिदन्यथासावनेकान्तः प्रतिषेधवचनं निर्णयः प्रकरणानुपूर्वं विधानं तस्य प्रातिलोम्यं विपर्यय इत्युक्तम्॥
अतिक्रान्ताय क्षणं परत्र वक्ष्यामि इत्यनागतावेक्षणमुभयतो हेतुदर्शनं संशयः तत्रातिशयवर्णनातिव्याख्यानं परमतमप्रतिषिद्धमनुमतं परैरसंमतः शब्दः स्वसंज्ञा लोके प्रती तमुदाहरणं निर्वचनं तद्युक्तिनिदर्शनं दृष्टान्त एवेति नियोग इदं वेदं वेति विकल्प इदं चेदं चेति समुश्चयोत्र यदनिर्दिष्टं युक्तिगम्यं तदू ह्यमिति ॥
प्रयोजनं संशयनिर्णयौ च व्याख्याविशेषो गुणलाघवश्च ॥
कृतव्युदासो कृतशासनं च सांवर्तिको धर्मगुणोष्टकश्च ॥
3.1.m:
3.6
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now, these are the hermeneutic devices (tantrayukti): the topic (adhikaraṇa), connection (yoga), word-meaning (padārtha), purpose of reason (hetvartha), brief statement (uddeśa), detailed statement (nirdeśa), local application (pradeśa), extended application (atideśa), exception (apavarga), sentence-completion (vākyaśeṣa), presumption (arthāpatti), context (prasaṅga), certainty (ekānta), uncertainty (naikānta), prima facie view (pūrvapakṣa), conclusive determination (nirṇaya), prescription (vidhāna), synonym (paryāya), reference to the past (atītakrāntāvekṣaṇa), doubt (saṃśaya), explanation (vyākhyāna), assent (anumati), special nomenclature (svasaṃjñā), etymology (nirvacana), illustrative example (dṛṣṭānta), disjunction (viyoga), option (vikalpa), and conjunction (samuccaya).
There, topic is that by which the sentence's meaning is joined together; connection is that meaning which is the modified word of a sūtra; word-meaning is that; purpose of reason is the establishment of an object by logical reasoning from another [source].
Brief statement is an abbreviated expression; detailed statement is an expanded expression; "precisely thus" is instruction; "for this reason" is assigned reason; local application is the establishment of a present matter through a future one; […] exception is that by which a meaning is concluded;
sentence-completion is [accomplished] by supplying an ellipsis; presumption is what follows necessarily from what has not been explicitly stated; context is what is mentioned as part of a topic and then stated again through some parenthetical relevance; certainty is that which holds true everywhere; uncertainty is that which holds true in some cases but otherwise elsewhere; conclusive determination is a statement of refutation; prescription is the ordered arrangement of a topic, and its inversion is called contrary.
Reference to the past is [such]; reference to the future is saying "I shall explain later"; doubt is seeing arguments on both sides; explanation is the detailed description thereof; assent is another's doctrine that is unrefuted; special nomenclature is a word not agreed upon by others; etymology is an example well known in common parlance; illustrative example is the display of that logic; option is saying "either this or that"; conjunction is saying "this and that"; and that which is unstated here but comprehensible through reasoning is to be inferred.
The purpose, doubt and conclusive determination, specific explanation and brevity of qualities, / the rejection of what has been done, the prescription of what has not been done, and the eightfold quality of dharma conducive to dissolution.

3.2.s:
3.7
.. mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi tava prākṛtalakṣaṇam ..
ṛ ṛṝ lṛ lṝ na saṃtyatra naṣmā na ca maṣāvubhau .. 1 ..
3.2.d:
3.7
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि तव प्राकृतलक्षणम् ॥
ऋ ऋॠ लृ लॄ न संत्यत्र नष्मा न च मषावुभौ ॥ 1 ॥
3.2.m:
3.7
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Now next I will declare to you the characteristics of Prākṛt: / here there are no ṛ, ṝ, lṛ, or lṝ, nor any sibilants [ṣ and ś], nor both ma and ṣa.

3.2.s:
sakārahīnā ca tathā nāsikyāśca tathā nṛpa ..
rephaśca śayavā rājan saṃyoge nāsti karhicit .. 2 ..
3.2.d:
सकारहीना च तथा नासिक्याश्च तथा नृप ॥
रेफश्च शयवा राजन् संयोगे नास्ति कर्हिचित् ॥ 2 ॥
3.2.m: And likewise it is devoid of the sa-sound, as well as nasals, O king; / and the repha [r] as well as śa, ya, and va, O king, never occur in a conjunct consonant.

3.2.s:
ekāraśca tathaukāraḥ padamadhye mahābalaḥ ..
dṛḍhayoge vakārotra ḍagayoge tathaiva ca ..3..
3.2.d:
एकारश्च तथौकारः पदमध्ये महाबलः ॥
दृढयोगे वकारोत्र डगयोगे तथैव च ॥3॥
3.2.m: Likewise e and o in the middle of a word are very strong; / in a dṛḍha-conjunct, va occurs here, and likewise in a ḍaga-conjunct.

3.2.s:
gayayoge gakāro'tra lopa māyāti nityadā ..
damau yuktau pṛthak kṛtvā dumau kāryau tathaiva ca .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
गययोगे गकारोऽत्र लोप मायाति नित्यदा ॥
दमौ युक्तौ पृथक् कृत्वा दुमौ कार्यौ तथैव च ॥ 4 ॥
3.2.m: Here, in a conjunction of ga and ya, the sound ga is constantly elided; / having separated a conjunct of da and ma, they should likewise be made into du and ma.

3.2.s:
ṛtayoge dakārasyāttakārastvabhidhīyate ..
kakāraḥ padamadhyotra vaktavyo halvivarjitaḥ .. 5 ..
3.2.d:
ऋतयोगे दकारस्यात्तकारस्त्वभिधीयते ॥
ककारः पदमध्योत्र वक्तव्यो हल्विवर्जितः ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m: In a conjunction of ṛ and ta, da should become ta, so it is said; / the sound ka in the middle of a word must be pronounced here devoid of a consonant.

3.2.s:
nakārasya ṇakāraḥ syātkṣakārasya kha iṣyate ..
takāraśca thakāraśca jñakāraśca ṇa eva ca .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
नकारस्य णकारः स्यात्क्षकारस्य ख इष्यते ॥
तकारश्च थकारश्च ज्ञकारश्च ण एव च ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m: For na there should be ṇa; for kṣa, kha is desired; / and ta, tha, and jña [become] ṇa alone.

3.2.s:
kvacitkvacitsyā ttadā hakāraśca tathā kvacit ..
kṣakārasya tu vaktavyaṃ vāṃkārasya ha iṣyate .. 7..
3.2.d:
क्वचित्क्वचित्स्या त्तदा हकारश्च तथा क्वचित् ॥
क्षकारस्य तु वक्तव्यं वांकारस्य ह इष्यते ॥ 7॥
3.2.m: In some places there should be ta, and in some places likewise ha; / but for kṣa it must be spoken, and for va, ha is desired.

3.2.s:
cakārasya chakāraḥ sthātyukare hal ca lupyate ..
yukte ṣakāre taddhībhe hakāro'pi vidhīyate .. 8 ..
3.2.d:
चकारस्य छकारः स्थात्युकरे हल् च लुप्यते ॥
युक्ते षकारे तद्धीभे हकारोऽपि विधीयते ॥ 8 ॥
3.2.m: For ca, cha remains, and in the case of u, the consonant is elided; / when ṣa is combined […], ha is also prescribed.

3.2.s:
caturtho nātra vijñeyā na ca dvivacanaṃ kvacit ..
padādau yo guruḥ sotra laghureva vidhīyate .. 9 ..
3.2.d:
चतुर्थो नात्र विज्ञेया न च द्विवचनं क्वचित् ॥
पदादौ यो गुरुः सोत्र लघुरेव विधीयते ॥ 9 ॥
3.2.m: A fourth [aspirated consonant] is not to be recognized here, nor anywhere a dual form; / that which is heavy at the beginning of a word is prescribed here as only light.

3.2.s:
dvimātrametaduddiṣṭaṃ madhyā prākṛtalakṣaṇam ..
prayogādanukartavyo vistaro hyativistaraḥ ..3.7.10..
3.2.d:
द्विमात्रमेतदुद्दिष्टं मध्या प्राकृतलक्षणम् ॥
प्रयोगादनुकर्तव्यो विस्तरो ह्यतिविस्तरः ॥3.7.10॥
3.2.m: This summary of the characteristics of Prākṛt has been stated in brief; / an elaboration, being excessively extensive, is to be followed from usage.

3.2.s:
deśeṣu deśeṣu pṛthagvibhinnaṃ na śakyate lakṣaṇatastu vaktum ..
lokeṣu yatsyādapabhraṣṭasaṃjñaṃ jñeyaṃ hi taddeśavidodhikāram .. 11 ..
3.8
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
devā divaukaso divyā gīrvāṇāstridaśāḥ surāḥ ..
harirjanārdano viṣṇurvāsudevastvadhokṣajaḥ .. 1 ..
nārāyaṇo hṛṣīkeśaścakrī garuḍavāhanaḥ ..
balaḥ saṃkarṣaṇo'nantaḥ śeṣastāladhvajo halī .. 2 ..
pradyumnaḥ kāmadevaśca cāpī makaraketanaḥ ..
khaṅgāyudho'niruddhaśca tathā vai ṛṣyaketanaḥ ..3..
lakṣmīḥ karīṣiṇī śrīśca tathā devī vibhāvarī ..
cakraḥ sudarśanaḥ proktaḥ śārṅgaṃ cāpastu vaiṣṇavam..4..
māheśvaraṃ pinākākhyaṃ vāruṇaṃ gaṇḍivaṃ bhavet ..
śākramājagavaṃ proktaṃ vajraḥ kuliśa ucyate .. 5 ..
vaiṣṇavī tu gadā proktā tathā kaumodakī nṛpa ..
halo lalāma ityuktaḥ sānandaṃ musalaṃ smṛtam .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
देशेषु देशेषु पृथग्विभिन्नं न शक्यते लक्षणतस्तु वक्तुम् ॥
लोकेषु यत्स्यादपभ्रष्टसंज्ञं ज्ञेयं हि तद्देशविदोधिकारम् ॥ 11 ॥
3.8
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
देवा दिवौकसो दिव्या गीर्वाणास्त्रिदशाः सुराः ॥
हरिर्जनार्दनो विष्णुर्वासुदेवस्त्वधोक्षजः ॥ 1 ॥
नारायणो हृषीकेशश्चक्री गरुडवाहनः ॥
बलः संकर्षणोऽनन्तः शेषस्तालध्वजो हली ॥ 2 ॥
प्रद्युम्नः कामदेवश्च चापी मकरकेतनः ॥
खङ्गायुधोऽनिरुद्धश्च तथा वै ऋष्यकेतनः ॥3॥
लक्ष्मीः करीषिणी श्रीश्च तथा देवी विभावरी ॥
चक्रः सुदर्शनः प्रोक्तः शार्ङ्गं चापस्तु वैष्णवम्॥4॥
माहेश्वरं पिनाकाख्यं वारुणं गण्डिवं भवेत् ॥
शाक्रमाजगवं प्रोक्तं वज्रः कुलिश उच्यते ॥ 5 ॥
वैष्णवी तु गदा प्रोक्ता तथा कौमोदकी नृप ॥
हलो ललाम इत्युक्तः सानन्दं मुसलं स्मृतम् ॥ 6 ॥

3.2.s:
pāñcajanyaḥ smṛtaḥ śaṅkhaḥ yaṃ bibharti janārdanaḥ ..
kare'sya kamalaṃ proktaṃ tathāstrālokyasaṃjñitam .. 7 ...
bhūmirvasuṃdharā pṛthvī kṣamā kṣoṇī dharā mahī ..
nabhaḥ khaṃ gaganaṃ caiva tathākāśaṃ hareḥ kramam .. 8 ..
tārkṣyaḥ suparṇo garuḍo hariketanavāhanaḥ ..
nāgānaṃto haladharaḥ śeṣaḥ tāladhvajī halī .. 9 ..
brahmā pitāmahaḥ śaṃbhuḥ svayaṃbhūrbhūtabhāvanaḥ ..
mahādevo bhavaḥ śaṃbhustryaṃbakaḥ pārvatīpatiḥ .. 3.8.10 ...
umā satī parvatajā menakājā tathocyate ..
bhadrakālī smṛtā durgā gaṇāśca pramathāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 11 ..
3.2.d:
पाञ्चजन्यः स्मृतः शङ्खः यं बिभर्ति जनार्दनः ॥
करेऽस्य कमलं प्रोक्तं तथास्त्रालोक्यसंज्ञितम् ॥ 7 ॥।
भूमिर्वसुंधरा पृथ्वी क्षमा क्षोणी धरा मही ॥
नभः खं गगनं चैव तथाकाशं हरेः क्रमम् ॥ 8 ॥
तार्क्ष्यः सुपर्णो गरुडो हरिकेतनवाहनः ॥
नागानंतो हलधरः शेषः तालध्वजी हली ॥ 9 ॥
ब्रह्मा पितामहः शंभुः स्वयंभूर्भूतभावनः ॥
महादेवो भवः शंभुस्त्र्यंबकः पार्वतीपतिः ॥ 3.8.10 ॥।
उमा सती पर्वतजा मेनकाजा तथोच्यते ॥
भद्रकाली स्मृता दुर्गा गणाश्च प्रमथाः स्मृताः ॥ 11 ॥

3.2.s:
vināyako gaṇapatiḥ kumāraḥ skanda iṣyate ...
indraḥ śakraḥ kauśikaśca puruhūtaḥ purandaraḥ .. 12 ..
3.2.d:
विनायको गणपतिः कुमारः स्कन्द इष्यते ॥।
इन्द्रः शक्रः कौशिकश्च पुरुहूतः पुरन्दरः ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m: Vināyaka is Gaṇapati; Kumāra is desired to be Skanda; / Indra is Śakra, Kauśika, Puruhūta, Purandara;

3.2.s:
agnirvaiśvānaro vahnirjātavedo hutāśanaḥ ..
vivasvato yamaścaiva kīnāśa pretanāyakaḥ .. 13 ..
3.2.d:
अग्निर्वैश्वानरो वह्निर्जातवेदो हुताशनः ॥
विवस्वतो यमश्चैव कीनाश प्रेतनायकः ॥ 13 ॥
3.2.m: Agni, Vaiśvānara, Vahni, Jātavedas, Hutāśana; / Yama the son of Vivasvat, Kīnāśa, leader of the departed (preta);

3.2.s:
virūpākṣo nirṛtiśca tathā rātriṃcarādhipaḥ ..
yādasāmīśvaro devaḥ pracetā varuṇoṃbupaḥ ..14..
3.2.d:
विरूपाक्षो निरृतिश्च तथा रात्रिंचराधिपः ॥
यादसामीश्वरो देवः प्रचेता वरुणोंबुपः ॥14॥
3.2.m: Virūpākṣa, Nirṛti, and likewise the lord of the night-wanderers; / the god who is the lord of aquatic creatures, Pracetas, Varuṇa, Ambupa;

3.2.s:
toyamaṃbu jalaṃ cāpaḥ pānīyaṃ salilaṃ payaḥ ..
vāyuḥ samīraṇo vātaḥ pāvanaḥ sarvago'nilaḥ .. 15 ..
3.2.d:
तोयमंबु जलं चापः पानीयं सलिलं पयः ॥
वायुः समीरणो वातः पावनः सर्वगोऽनिलः ॥ 15 ॥
3.2.m: Toya, ambu, jala, ap, pānīya, salila, payas [for water]; / Vāyu, Samīraṇa, Vāta, Pāvana, the all-pervading, Anila [for the wind];

3.2.s:
rājarājo dhanādhyakṣastathaivaiḍaviḍaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
īśānaḥ śaṅkaraḥ śarvaḥ tathā paśupatiḥ śivaḥ .. 16 ..
3.2.d:
राजराजो धनाध्यक्षस्तथैवैडविडः स्मृतः ॥
ईशानः शङ्करः शर्वः तथा पशुपतिः शिवः ॥ 16 ॥
3.2.m: Rājarāja, the superintendent of wealth, and likewise remembered as Aiḍaviḍa; / Īśāna, Śaṅkara, Śarva, and likewise Paśupati, Śiva;

3.2.s:
nāsatyāvaśvinau proktau vasavo vasusaṃjñitāḥ ..
tathaivāṃgiraso nāgā viśve satrāgrabhojinaḥ .. 17 ..
3.2.d:
नासत्यावश्विनौ प्रोक्तौ वसवो वसुसंज्ञिताः ॥
तथैवांगिरसो नागा विश्वे सत्राग्रभोजिनः ॥ 17 ॥
3.2.m: The two Aśvins are declared to be Nāsatyas; the Vasus are called the Vasus; / likewise the Āṅgirases, the serpents (nāgas), and the Viśvedevas, who eat the first offerings at sacrificial sessions.

3.2.s:
vṛṣabhāvagamāruddha bhṛgavo maruto matāḥ ..
sādhyā dharmasutāḥ proktā ādityā kaśyapātmajāḥ .. 18 ..
3.2.d:
वृषभावगमारुद्ध भृगवो मरुतो मताः ॥
साध्या धर्मसुताः प्रोक्ता आदित्या कश्यपात्मजाः ॥ 18 ॥
3.2.m: The Bhṛgus and the Maruts are known as [...]; / the Sādhyas are declared to be the sons of Dharma, and the Ādityas the sons of Kaśyapa.

3.2.s:
māruto mātariśvāno grahāstribhuvaneśvarāḥ ..
nakṣatrāṇi tathā tāni ṛkṣāṇi ca uḍūni ca .. 19 ..

3.2.m: The wind [is named] Māruta and Mātariśvan; the planets are the lords of the three worlds; / and the asterisms are called nakṣatras, ṛkṣas, and uḍus.

आदित्यो भास्करः सूर्यः सविता रविरर्यमा ॥
चन्द्रः शीतकरः सोमः शशांको मृगलाञ्छनः ॥ 3.8.20 ॥
3.2.m: The sun is Āditya, Bhāskara, Sūrya, Savitṛ, Ravi, and Aryaman; / the moon is Candra, Śītakara, Soma, Śaśāṅka, and Mṛgalāñchana.

वक्रः क्षितिसुतो भौमो बुधो ज्ञः सोमनन्दनः ॥
बृहस्पतिर्गुरुर्जीवः शुक्र आस्फुजिरेव च ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m: Mars is Vakra, Kṣitisuta, and Bhauma; Mercury is Budha, Jña, and Somanandana; / Jupiter is Bṛhaspati, Guru, and Jīva; Venus is Śukra and Āsphujit.

3.2.m: The fifth is proclaimed as Sāraṇa, expert in churning; / demons are asuras, dānavas, and daityas; gandharvas are the divine leaders.

यक्षाः पुण्यजनाः प्रोक्ता यातुधानाश्च राक्षसाः ॥
अदृश्याश्च तथा भूताः पिशाचाः पिशिताशनाः ॥ 23 ॥
3.2.m: Yakṣas are called puṇyajanas; and yātudhānas are rākṣasas; / ghosts are invisible spirits; piśācas are eaters of flesh.

kinnarākhyāḥ kiṃpuruṣā nāgāḥ kadrusutā matāḥ ..
siddhā vidyādharā proktā devarāmāstathāpsarāḥ .. 24..
3.2.d:
किन्नराख्याः किंपुरुषा नागाः कद्रुसुता मताः ॥
सिद्धा विद्याधरा प्रोक्ता देवरामास्तथाप्सराः ॥ 24॥
3.2.m: Kinnaras are named kimpuruṣas; serpents are considered the sons of Kadru; / siddhas are called vidyādharas; divine women are apsarases.

proktāḥ saptarṣayo loke tathā citraśikhaṃḍinaḥ .. 25 ..

महर्षयो भूतकृतः तथा ब्रह्मर्षयोमलाः ॥
प्रोक्ताः सप्तर्षयो लोके तथा चित्रशिखंडिनः ॥ 25 ॥
3.2.m: Great seers are the creators of beings, and stainless are the brahmin seers; / the seven seers are known in the world as the Citraśikhaṇḍins.

आशा दिशस्तथा काष्ठा भचक्रं भगणं स्मृतम् ॥ 26 ॥
3.2.m: The pole star is declared to be Dhruva, Sthāsnu, and Kṛkalāsa; / āśā, diś, and kāṣṭhā [signify] directions; the zodiac is known as bhacakra and bhagaṇa.

3.2.d:
कृतानि शास्त्राणि नरेन्द्र पूर्वैः स्मृतिस्तथोक्ता श्रुतिरेव वेदः ॥
सम्यग्यदाचारमिति प्रदिष्टं वृत्तं हि यच्छास्त्रविदां नरेन्द्र ॥ 27 ॥
3.9
संवत्सरोऽब्दो वर्षं च समा हायन एव च ॥
दिवसो वासरश्चैव दिनं चाहस्तथैव च ॥ 1 ॥
दोषा विभावरी रात्रिः शर्वरी यामिनी क्षपा ॥
संधिः प्रोक्ता तथा सन्ध्या अन्धकारं तमः स्मृतम् ॥ 2 ॥
चन्द्रिका च तथा ज्योत्स्ना चैत्रो मधुरिति स्मृतः॥।
वैशाखो माधवः प्रोक्तः शुचिर्ज्येष्ठ उदाहृतः ॥ 3 ॥
शुक्लः प्रोक्तस्तथाषाढो नभः श्रावण इष्यते ॥
प्रौष्ठपादो नभस्यश्च इषश्चाश्वयुजः स्मृतः ॥ 4 ॥
ऊर्जाख्यः कार्तिकः प्रोक्तो मार्गशीर्षः सहस्तथा ॥
सहस्यः पौष इत्युक्तो माघः स्यात्तप एव च ॥ 5 ॥
फाल्गुनश्च तपस्याख्यो मासो यदु कुलोद्वह ॥
तुलामेषगते भानौ विषुवद्दिनमुच्यते ॥ 6 ॥
3.2.m:
The treatises, O king, were composed by the ancients; Smṛti is called tradition, and Śruti is the Veda; / that conduct which belongs to the knowers of the treatises, O king, is indeed designated as proper practice.
3.9 / A year is saṃvatsara, abda, varṣa, samā, and hāyana; / a day is divasa, vāsara, dina, and ahan.
Night is doṣā, vibhāvarī, rātri, śarvarī, yāminī, and kṣapā; / twilight is proclaimed as saṃdhi and sandhyā; darkness is known as andhakāra and tamas.
Moonlight is candrikā and jyotsnā; Caitra is known as Madhu; / Vaiśākha is called Mādhava; Jyeṣṭha is spoken of as Śuci.
Āṣāḍha is proclaimed as Śukla; Śrāvaṇa is acknowledged as Nabhas; / Bhādrapada is Nabhasya; and Āśvina is known as Iṣa.
Kārtika is called Ūrja; Mārgaśīrṣa is Sahas; / Pauṣa is spoken of as Sahasya; and Māgha is Tapas.
And Phālguna is the month named Tapasya, O scion of the Yadu race; / when the sun enters Libra and Aries, it is called the equinox day.

3.2.d:
धन्वतो मिथुनान्तश्च अयने सोस्य दक्षिणे ॥
मेषान्ते च तुलान्ते च युगादिदिवसौ स्मृतौ ॥ 7 ॥
तथा विष्णुपदं प्रोक्तं कुलीरमकरान्तयोः ॥
कन्या मिथुनमीनानां प्रवेशे धनुषस्तथा ॥ 8 ॥
षडशीतिमुखं नाम ज्ञेयं दिन चतुष्टयम् ॥
रश्मिर्गभस्तिर्भद्रा च करो दीधितिरेव च ॥ 9 ॥
सूर्योदयास्तमययोः स दीर्घः परिधिर्भवेत् ॥
तिर्यग्गतां मेघराजीं तदेव परिघो भवेत् ॥ 3.9.10 ॥
तदेव दण्डसंस्थानो मेघो दण्डोभिधीयते ॥
शक्रचापं शक्रधनुः तद्दीर्घं रोहितं भवेत् ॥1 1॥
तदेव दण्डसंस्थानो मेघो दण्डोऽभि धीयते ॥
शक्रं चापं शक्रधनुः तद्दीर्घं रोहितं मतम्॥12॥
तत्पीतःमथाल्पं क दुपास्यं प्रतिसूर्यकम्॥
चन्द्रार्कयोर्मेघराजितपरिवेषस्तु मण्डलात् ॥13॥
3.2.m:
From Sagittarius to the end of Gemini is his southern course; / the end of Aries and the end of Libra are known as the days marking the beginning of an era.
Likewise, the step of Viṣṇu is proclaimed at the ends of Cancer and Capricorn; / at the entry of the sun into Virgo, Gemini, Pisces, and Sagittarius,
the four days are to be known by the name of ṣaḍaśītimukha; / a ray [of light] is raśmi, gabhasti, bhadrā, kara, and dīdhiti.
At sunrise and sunset, that long [halo] becomes a paridhi; / that very streak of clouds lying crosswise becomes a parigha.
A cloud resembling a staff is called daṇḍa; / Indra's rainbow is Śakracāpa and Śakradhanus; when elongated, it is a rohita.
A cloud resembling a staff is called daṇḍa; / Indra's bow is Śakracāpa and Śakradhanus; when elongated, it is considered a rohita.
When yellow and small, it is [...] a mock sun; / the streak of clouds encircling the disc of the moon and sun is a pariveṣa.

anityaḥ saśikho dṛṣṭaḥ tārakaḥ keturiṣyate ..14..
agnivarṇā tu diṅmṛṣṭā digdāha iti viśrutaḥ ..
nagaraṃ śūnyato dṛṣṭaṃ gandharvanagaraṃ smṛtam .. 15..

yatoyato yavaṃ dṛṣṭiḥ kathitā mṛgatṛṣṇikā .. 16..
megho ghanaṃ vāridaṃ ca jīmūtaṃ ca balāhakam ..
stanitaṃ garjitaṃ vidyād vṛṣṭiḥ proktāḥ pravarṣaṇe .. 17 ..
āsāro vegavadvarṣaṃ pṛṣato maṃda ucyate ..
dṛśyamāne tathā sūrye divyaṃ proktaṃ ca varṣaṇam..18..

3.2.d:
स्वर्गाच्छुभफले क्षीणे पतन्नुल्केति कथ्यते ॥
अनित्यः सशिखो दृष्टः तारकः केतुरिष्यते ॥14॥
अग्निवर्णा तु दिङ्मृष्टा दिग्दाह इति विश्रुतः ॥
नगरं शून्यतो दृष्टं गन्धर्वनगरं स्मृतम् ॥ 15॥
निर्घातं स्तनितं प्रोक्तं विना मेघनिदर्शनात् ॥
यतोयतो यवं दृष्टिः कथिता मृगतृष्णिका ॥ 16॥
मेघो घनं वारिदं च जीमूतं च बलाहकम् ॥
स्तनितं गर्जितं विद्याद् वृष्टिः प्रोक्ताः प्रवर्षणे ॥ 17 ॥
आसारो वेगवद्वर्षं पृषतो मंद उच्यते ॥
दृश्यमाने तथा सूर्ये दिव्यं प्रोक्तं च वर्षणम्॥18॥
दृश्यमाने तथा चन्द्रे सामृतं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
वात्या वातसमुत्था स्यान्नीहारं तम उच्यते ॥19॥
शीकराख्यमवश्यायं तुषारस्तुहिनं हिमम् ॥
विद्युत्तडित्तथा लोला चञ्चला च शतह्रदा ॥ 3.9.20 ॥
समुद्राश्चाम्बुनिधयः सागरा लवणोदकाः ॥
नद्यः कुटिलगामिन्यो निम्नगाः सरितस्तथा ॥ 21 ॥
3.2.m:
Falling from heaven when auspicious merit is exhausted, it is called a meteor; / seen transiently with a crest, a star is recognized as a comet.
A horizon wiped with the colour of fire is renowned as a fire-glow of the quarters; / a city seen in empty space is known as a city of the gandharvas.
Thunder without the sight of clouds is proclaimed as a thunderclap; / the illusory sight of water appearing here and there is called a mirage.
A cloud is megha, ghana, vārida, jīmūta, and balāhaka; / one should know thunder as stanita and garjita; rain is spoken of as pravarṣaṇa.
A torrential rain is āsāra; a gentle drizzle is called pṛṣata; / while the sun is visible, rain is proclaimed as divine.
While the moon is visible, it is declared to be endowed with nectar; / a cyclone is born of wind; mist is called darkness.
Dew is called śīkara and avaśyāya; frost is tuṣāra, tuhina, and hima; / lightning is vidyut, taḍit, lolā, cañcalā, and śatahradā.
Oceans are samudras, ambunidhis, sāgaras, and salt waters; / rivers are winding streams, nimnagās, and sarits.

3.2.d:
गङ्गाविष्णुपदी प्रोक्ता जाह्नवी त्रिपथा तथा ॥
कालिन्दी यमुना प्रोक्ता रेवा प्रोक्ता च नर्मदा ॥
विपाशा च सनन्दाख्या शतद्रुः शौरिसंज्ञिका ॥ 22॥
बुद्धिस्तथा सूर्य इति प्रदिष्टो भूतानि चोक्तानि तथेन्द्रियाणि ॥
वाणी तथोक्ता च सरस्वती च मनस्तथोक्तं नृप चन्द्रसंज्ञम् ॥ 23 ॥
3.10
॥ मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥ ॥
मनुष्यो मनुजश्चैव पुरुषः पुरुषस्तथा ॥
रामा योषित्तथा स्त्री च ललना च तथा स्मृता ॥ 1 ॥
वरारोहा पुरन्ध्रिश्च श्रेष्ठा सा मत्तकाशिनी ॥
ब्राह्मणश्च तथा विप्रो राजन्यः क्षत्रियो मतः ॥ 2 ॥
कीनाशश्च स्मृतो वैश्यः शूद्रश्चान्त्यज उच्यते ॥
चण्डालः पुक्ककः प्रोक्तो मातङ्गश्च तथोच्यते ॥ 3 ॥
हस्ती द्विप इभो दन्ती मातङ्गः कुञ्जरो गजः ॥
अश्वश्च तुरगः सप्तिर्हयो वाजी हरिस्तथा ॥ 4 ॥
गौरुक्षाच्छागलोऽजश्च उरभ्रोऽविस्तथोच्यते ॥ 5 ॥
3.2.m:
The Gaṅgā is called Viṣṇupadī, Jāhnavī, and Tripathā; / the Yamunā is called Kālindī; the Narmadā is called Revā; / the Vipāśā is named Sanandā; and the Śatadru is known as Śauri.
Intellect is proclaimed as the sun, and the elements are spoken of as the senses; / speech is proclaimed as Sarasvatī, and the mind, O king, is called the moon.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: / A man is manuṣya, manuja, puruṣa, and pūruṣa; / a woman is known as rāmā, yoṣit, strī, and lalanā.
An excellent woman is varārohā, purandhrī, and mattakāśinī; / a brāhmaṇa is vipra; a kṣatriya is regarded as rājanya.
A vaiśya is known as kīnāśa; a śūdra is called antyaja; / an outcaste is caṇḍāla, pukkasa, and is likewise called mātaṅga.
An elephant is hastin, dvipa, ibha, dantin, mātaṅga, kuñjara, and gaja; / a horse is aśva, turaga, sapti, haya, vājin, and hari.
A bull is go and ukṣan; a goat is chāgala and aja; / a ram is called urabhra and avi.

3.2.d:
असिर्विशसनः खड्गस्तीक्ष्ण धारो दुरासदः ॥
श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्माधारस्तथाष्टमः ॥ 6 ॥
सुवर्णं कनकं रुक्मं हेमं कार्तस्वरं तथा ॥
जाम्बूनदं तद्देवानां रूप्यं रजतमिष्यते ॥ 7 ॥
उदुम्बरं स्मृतं ताम्रमयोलोहं प्रकीर्तितम ॥
आरकूटं तथा रीती रत्नं माणिक्यमुच्यते ॥ 8 ॥
आतपत्रं स्मृतं छत्रं कम्बुः शंख उदाहृतः ॥
पङ्कजं कमलं पद्मं पुण्डरीकं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥9॥
तथा तामरसं चैव शतपत्रं तु दैवतम् ॥
इन्दीवरं चोत्पलं स्यात्कह्लारं शुक्लमेव तत्॥3.10.10॥
संग्राममाजिर्युद्धं च जन्यमाहव एव च ॥
दानं संवननं प्रोक्तं विवाहो विनिवेशनम् ॥11॥
पत्नी भार्या तथा जाया सुतः पुत्रस्तनूद्भवः ॥
माता जनित्री जननी जनिता जनकः पिता ॥ 12 ॥
3.2.m:
A sword is asi, viśasana, khaḍga, tīkṣṇadhāra, durāsada, / śrīgarbha, vijaya, and eighth, dharmādhāra.
Gold is suvarṇa, kanaka, rukma, hema, and kārtasvara; / that of the gods is jāmbūnada; silver is designated as rūpya and rajata.
Copper is known as udumbara; iron is proclaimed as ayas and loha; / brass is ārakūṭa and rīti; a jewel is called māṇikya.
The parasol is called *ātapatra* or *chatra*; the conch is referred to as *kambu* or *śaṅkha*. / The lotus is known as *paṅkaja*, *kamala*, *padma*, [and] *puṇḍarīka*,
as well as *tāmarasa*, and *śatapatra*, which belongs to the gods; / the blue water-lily is *indīvara* and *utpala*, and *kahlāra* is indeed the white [water-lily].
Battle is *saṃgrāma*, *āji*, *yuddha*, *janya*, and *āhava*; / a gift is declared to be *dāna* and *saṃvanana*; marriage is *vivāha* and *viniveśana*.
Wife is *patnī*, *bhāryā*, and *jāyā*; son is *suta*, *putra*, and *tanūdbhava*; / mother is *mātā*, *janitrī*, and *jananī*; father is *janitā*, *janaka*, and *pitā*.

kṣayaṃ ca bhavanaṃ proktaṃ mandiraṃ gṛhameva ca ..
bhāṇḍāgāraḥ smṛtaḥ kośo dhanvanaṃ guptiriṣyate .. 13..
vāhanaṃ patrasaṃjñaṃ syādamatraṃ pātramucyate ..
vardhamānaṃ śarāve syāccāpaṃ ca dhanurucyate..14..
sāyakaśca śaraḥ prokta iṣurbāṇaḥ śilīmukhaḥ ..
hastamocyaḥ sa evokto bṛhantaścaiva tovaraḥ..15..
puṣpaprakaramityuktamupakāraṃ narādhipa..
bālavyajanamapyuktaṃ tathā cāramasaṃjñitam..16..
mṛjā śobhā vinirdiṣṭā alaṅkāro vibhūṣaṇam ..
prasādhanaṃ maṇḍanaṃ syādbalaḥ sāra udāhṛtaḥ ..17..
arbhakaśca smṛto bālo bālaścāśvaḥ kiśorakaḥ..
hastī kalabha ityukto vatsaścokṣā prakīrtitaḥ .. 18 ..
sarvathā keśarī siṃhaḥ śārdūlo vyāghra ucyate ..
vipinaṃ nirjanaṃ proktamajiraṃ syādgṛhāṅgaṇam .. .. 19 ..
upanīya dadadvedamācāryaḥ sa udāhṛtaḥ ..
ekadeśamupādhyāyo ṛtvigyajñakṛducyate .. 3.10.20..
3.2.d:
क्षयं च भवनं प्रोक्तं मन्दिरं गृहमेव च ॥
भाण्डागारः स्मृतः कोशो धन्वनं गुप्तिरिष्यते ॥ 13॥
वाहनं पत्रसंज्ञं स्यादमत्रं पात्रमुच्यते ॥
वर्धमानं शरावे स्याच्चापं च धनुरुच्यते॥14॥
सायकश्च शरः प्रोक्त इषुर्बाणः शिलीमुखः ॥
हस्तमोच्यः स एवोक्तो बृहन्तश्चैव तोवरः॥15॥
पुष्पप्रकरमित्युक्तमुपकारं नराधिप॥
बालव्यजनमप्युक्तं तथा चारमसंज्ञितम्॥16॥
मृजा शोभा विनिर्दिष्टा अलङ्कारो विभूषणम् ॥
प्रसाधनं मण्डनं स्याद्बलः सार उदाहृतः ॥17॥
अर्भकश्च स्मृतो बालो बालश्चाश्वः किशोरकः॥
हस्ती कलभ इत्युक्तो वत्सश्चोक्षा प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 18 ॥
सर्वथा केशरी सिंहः शार्दूलो व्याघ्र उच्यते ॥
विपिनं निर्जनं प्रोक्तमजिरं स्याद्गृहाङ्गणम् ॥ ॥ 19 ॥
उपनीय ददद्वेदमाचार्यः स उदाहृतः ॥
एकदेशमुपाध्यायो ऋत्विग्यज्ञकृदुच्यते ॥ 3.10.20॥
3.2.m:
A dwelling is called *kṣaya*, *bhavana*, *mandira*, and *gṛha*; / a storehouse is called *bhāṇḍāgāra* and *kośa*; a hiding place is considered *dhanvana* and *gupti*.
A conveyance has the name *vāhana* and *patra*; a vessel is called *amatra* and *pātra*; / a shallow dish is called *vardhamāna* and *śarāva*; a bow is called *cāpa* and *dhanus*.
An arrow is called *sāyaka*, *śara*, *iṣu*, *bāṇa*, and *śilīmukha*; / that which is released by the hand is also spoken of as *bṛhanta* and *tovara*.
A shower of flowers is called *puṣpaprakara* and *upakāra*, O king; / a fly-whisk of hair is also named *bālavyajana* as well as *cāmara*.
Beauty is designated as *mṛjā* and *śobhā*; ornament is *alaṅkāra* and *vibhūṣaṇa*; / decoration is *prasādhana* and *maṇḍana*; strength is declared to be *bala* and *sāra*.
A child is called *arbhaka* and *bāla*; a young horse is a *kiśoraka*; / an elephant [calf] is called *kalabha*; and a [young] bull is called *vatsa* and *ukṣan*.
In every case, a lion is *keśarin* and *siṃha*; a tiger is called *śārdūla* and *vyāghra*; / an uninhabited [forest] is called *vipina* and *nirjana*; a courtyard of a house is *ajira* and *gṛhāṅgaṇa*.
He who initiates and imparts the Veda is declared to be an *ācārya*; / he who teaches a portion [of the Veda] is an *upādhyāya*; the priest who performs the sacrifice is called an *ṛtvij*.

3.2.s:
sāṃvatsaro jyautiṣavid vṛto bhavati bhūbhujā ..
tasyaiva yajñakṛdyastu sa purohita iṣyate .. 21..
amātyaśca smṛto mantrī deśo nicaya ucyate ..
rājā narendro nṛpatistathaiva siṃhāsanaṃ tasya tathāsanaṃ syāt ..
kṣattā pratīhāra iti pradiṣṭastaddhastadaṇḍaḥ kathitaṃ tu vetram .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
सांवत्सरो ज्यौतिषविद् वृतो भवति भूभुजा ॥
तस्यैव यज्ञकृद्यस्तु स पुरोहित इष्यते ॥ 21॥
अमात्यश्च स्मृतो मन्त्री देशो निचय उच्यते ॥
राजा नरेन्द्रो नृपतिस्तथैव सिंहासनं तस्य तथासनं स्यात् ॥
क्षत्ता प्रतीहार इति प्रदिष्टस्तद्धस्तदण्डः कथितं तु वेत्रम् ॥ 22 ॥
3.2.m:
The astrologer versed in astronomy is chosen by the king; / he who performs sacrifices for that very [king] is considered the *purohita*.
The minister is called *amātya* and *mantrin*; a heap is called *deśa* and *nicaya*; / a king is *rājā*, *narendra*, and *nṛpati*; his throne is *siṃhāsana* and *āsana*; / the door-keeper is designated as *kṣattṛ* and *pratīhāra*; the staff in his hand is called *vetra*.

कुटिः खोरी दया ज्योत्स्ना सीमा वेणिस्तथैव वाक् ॥3 ॥

दरः प्रावृट् चाचमनी स्थूणा चूडा सिरा वसा ॥4॥

3.3.s:

vidyutkakṣā saridvallīriṣīkā rajjuriṣṭakā .. 5 ..

विद्युत्कक्षा सरिद्वल्लीरिषीका रज्जुरिष्टका ॥ 5 ॥

chāyā camūrvālukā ca tathā vidyudvipatsarit ..6..

दिग्भूर्भूमिर्मही क्षोणी क्षपा चैव वसुन्धरा॥
छाया चमूर्वालुका च तथा विद्युद्विपत्सरित् ॥6॥
3.3.m: *diś*, *bhū*, *bhūmi*, *mahī*, *kṣoṇī*, and *kṣapā*, and *vasundharā*, / *chāyā*, *camū*, and *vālukā*, as well as *vidyut*, *vipad*, *sarit*,

3.3.s:

kalā ca mekhalā jvālā senā dadrurvalī samā ..7..

इरा सम्पदवापश्च लीला वेला तला शिला ॥
कला च मेखला ज्वाला सेना दद्रुर्वली समा ॥7॥

3.3.s:
jyā ca mlānistathā hāniḥ śāṭī svāhā tathaiva gīḥ ..
dhīrvṛddhirdhūḥ kṣamā buddhiḥ kṣutkṣamāśīḥ savālukā..8..

धीर्वृद्धिर्धूः क्षमा बुद्धिः क्षुत्क्षमाशीः सवालुका॥8॥

3.3.s:
viṃśaternavatiryāvatkroḍāsvaduśirodharā ..
māyā ca śaṣkulī jihvā ghaṭotkā snāyureva ca ..9..

विंशतेर्नवतिर्यावत्क्रोडास्वदुशिरोधरा ॥
माया च शष्कुली जिह्वा घटोत्का स्नायुरेव च ॥9॥

लेखा जरा तथा पङ्क्तिस्त्रेता प्रावृडरोचका ॥
लाक्षा कण्डूः प्रियंगुश्च माण्डिका कटिरौषधिः ॥ 3.11.10 ॥

niḥśreṇiḥ pṛtanā dīptirnidrā tandrā guhā ruciḥ .. 11 ..

ऋक्स्फुलिङ्गा कलिः शय्या कोटिः कन्या च नालिका॥

maṃjūṣā parṣadaścaiva patākā kākinī kṛpā .. 12 ..

मंजूषा पर्षदश्चैव पताका काकिनी कृपा ॥ 12 ॥

3.3.s:
pelā caiva samaṃjiṣṭhā bherī nemirmanaḥśilā ..
darvī sthālī sabhā vīciḥ sthalī caiva samañjarī ..13..

3.3.s:
vallarī mandurā lākṣā sūcī cādhiṣaṇā śamī ..
makṣikā vikṛtiryūkā śikhā śākhā tathāṭavī .. 14 ..

वल्लरी मन्दुरा लाक्षा सूची चाधिषणा शमी ॥

3.3.s:
strīvṛttayaste kathitā mayaite śabdāḥ samāsastvayamatra rājan ..
idaṃ tamānantyamuśaṃti sarvaṃ strīvācakaṃ śabdamuśanti dhīrāḥ .. 15 ..

mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yaduvaṃśavivardhana ..
tava puṃvācakāñśabdāñśṛṇu tāngadato mama .. 1 ..
rājā kṛtākṣamūrdhātmā pāyuśleṣmāśmapūraṇaḥ ..
majjā plīhā ca kathitā nātādyaskāḥ pumarthakāḥ .. 2 ..
vṛtraḥ putrastathā mantrastathaivāmantra iṣyate ..
puṃsi rāśirmuhurtaśca māsaḥ pakṣo'bdavatsarau .. 3 ..
ṛtuḥ kālo giriḥ śailaḥ śiloccayattugācalāḥ ..
surāsurāṇāṃ saṃjñāśca yāśca proktā mahodadheḥ .. 4 ..
saṃvatsaraśca divaso graho vāsara eva ca ..
paryāyaḥ paṅkaśarayorarinistriṃśayorapi .. 5 ..
putraparyāyaśabdāśca pitṛparyāyasaṃyutāḥ ..
kaṇṭhabāhvostathā saṃjñāḥ stanakeśaradasya ca ..6..

स्त्रीवृत्तयस्ते कथिता मयैते शब्दाः समासस्त्वयमत्र राजन् ॥
इदं तमानन्त्यमुशंति सर्वं स्त्रीवाचकं शब्दमुशन्ति धीराः ॥ 15 ॥
3.12
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि यदुवंशविवर्धन ॥
तव पुंवाचकाञ्शब्दाञ्शृणु तान्गदतो मम ॥ 1 ॥
राजा कृताक्षमूर्धात्मा पायुश्लेष्माश्मपूरणः ॥

*Rājā*, *kṛtākṣa*, *mūrdhan*, *ātman*, *pāyu*, *śleṣman*, *aśmapūraṇa*, / *majjan*, and *plīhan* are declared; words ending in *-n* and *-t* denote masculine meanings.

3.14 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The repeated placement of each single syllable, / for the sake of conveying meaning, was designated as alliteration (anuprāsa) by the ancients.
Done excessively, O king, it descends into vulgarity. / Words [repeated] in identical sequence, on the other hand, are declared as rhyme (yamaka).
That is desired at the beginning, in the middle, or at the end of a quarter-verse; / likewise, the [two varieties of] rhyme known as saṃdaṣṭaka and samudra are recognised.
A rhyme involving an entire quarter-verse is declared to be difficult to compose. / The equality of the object of comparison (upameya) with the standard of comparison (upamāna) is metaphor (rūpaka).
The heightened metaphor (rūpakābhyadhika) is that very same figure with one superior quality. / Contrast (vyatireka) is exemplified by a distinction in qualities,
and it is held to be another [variety] through qualities opposed to the standard of comparison. / Through words expressing two or three meanings, it is designated as pun (śleṣa).

3.3.d:
अन्यरूपस्य चार्थस्य कल्पना यान्यथा भवेत् ॥
उत्प्रेक्षाख्यो ह्यलङ्कारः कथितः स पुरातनैः॥7॥
उपन्यासस्तथान्यः स्यात्प्रस्तुताद्यः क्वचिद्भवेत्॥
ज्ञेयः सोर्थान्तरन्यासः पूर्वार्थानुगतो यदि ॥ 8 ॥
उपन्यासेन वान्यस्य यदन्यः परिकीर्त्यते ॥
उपन्यासमलङ्कारं तं नरेन्द्र प्रचक्षते ॥ 9 ॥
हेतुं विना वितततां प्राप्ता सा तु विभावना ॥
प्रोक्ता चातिशयोक्तिस्तु ह्यतुलैरुपमागुणैः ॥ 3.14.10 ॥
यथा स्वरूपकथनं स्वभावोक्तिः प्रकीर्तिता ॥
भूयसामुपदिष्टानां निर्देशः क्रमशस्तथा ॥ 11 ॥
यथासंख्यमिति प्रोक्तमलङ्कारः पुरातनैः ॥
विशेषप्रापणादुक्ता विशेषोक्तिस्तथा नृप ॥ 12 ॥
या क्रिया चान्यफलदा विरोधस्तु स इष्यते ॥
स्तुतिरूपेण या निन्दा निन्दास्तुतिरिहोच्यते ॥ 13 ॥
निन्दास्तुतिस्तथैवोक्ता निन्दारूपेण या स्तुतिः ॥
वस्तुना रूप्यमाणेन दर्शनं तन्निदर्शनम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.3.m:
And when a thing of one form is imagined as something otherwise, / that is declared by the ancients as the poetic figure called poetic fancy (utprekṣā).
Likewise, another statement may occur, distinct from what is under discussion; / that is to be known as corroboration (arthāntaranyāsa) if it conforms to the preceding sense.
Or when another matter is proclaimed by means of the statement of something else, / that, O lord of men, they call the poetic figure of statement (upanyāsa).
When an effect achieves expansion without an [apparent] cause, that is special indication (vibhāvanā). / And hyperbole (atiśayokti) is declared through incomparable qualities of comparison.
The description of a thing as it actually is, is proclaimed as natural description (svabhāvokti). / And the sequential presentation of several things that have been taught,
is named relative order (yathāsaṃkhya) as a poetic figure by the ancients. / Special mention (viśeṣokti), O king, is spoken of from the attainment of a specific excellence.
An action that yields a different fruit is held to be incongruity (virodha). / Reproach in the form of praise is called reproachful praise (nindāstuti) here;
praise in the form of reproach is likewise declared to be nindāstuti. / Illustration (nidarśana) is the showing [of a concept] through an object that depicts it.

3.15
मार्कण्डेय उवाच ॥
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां शास्त्रं स्यादुपदेशकम् ॥
पूर्वैराचरितं सद्भिर्धर्मकामार्थसाधकम् ॥ 1 ॥
मोक्षस्य यत्रोपन्यास इतिहासः स उच्यते ॥
तदेव काव्यमित्युक्तं चोपदेशं विना कृतम् ॥ 2 ॥
एकस्य चरितादेव तथा काव्यं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
निबद्धो यत्र राजेन्द्र नायकप्रतिनायकौ ॥3॥
प्रयाणोद्यतसंप्रेषयुद्धयुक्तं तदेव तु ॥
नायकाभ्युदयोपेतं महाकाव्यं तदिष्यते ॥4॥
वर्णयेच्च महाकाव्ये देशपत्तनपार्थिवान् ॥
ऋत्वद्रिनिम्नगाश्चैव तथा नारीश्च पार्थिव ॥5॥
वर्णनीयौ तथैवात्र नायकप्रतिनायकौ ॥
नायको धर्मविजयी सताम्पन्थानमाश्रितः॥6॥
3.3.m:
Where, O hero among men, a comparison occurs without [another object], such that it belongs to that very [subject] alone, / it is called self-comparison (ananvaya) by the ancients. Thus much has been declared to you, merely in brief.
3.15 / Mārkaṇḍeya said: / A treatise (śāstra) must be an instruction in dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation. / What was practiced by the virtuous of old, achieving dharma, pleasure, and wealth,
wherein an exposition of liberation is given, is called epic history (itihāsa). / That very same thing is declared to be poetry (kāvya) when composed without [direct] instruction.
Poetry is likewise proclaimed from the life of a single [hero] alone, / in which, O best of kings, a protagonist and an antagonist are composed.
That which is furnished with marches, readiness, envoys, and battles, / and endowed with the triumph of the protagonist, is held to be a court epic (mahākāvya).
And in a court epic one should describe countries, cities, and kings, / seasons, mountains, rivers, and likewise women, O king.
The protagonist and the antagonist should likewise be described here; / the protagonist must be victorious through dharma, adhering to the path of the good.

छन्दोविरहितं गद्यं शब्दशास्त्रविरोधि च ॥

तस्मादुल्लक्ष्यवाक्यार्थमप्रसिद्धाभिधानवत् ॥

विस्मये वाभ्यसूयायां भयशोकत्वरासु च ॥

दूतवाक्ये तथा स्वप्ने कार्यगत्या तथागते॥

ससंशयं न वक्तव्यं प्रतिज्ञारहितं तथा ॥
पूर्वापरविरुद्धं च यच्च लोकविगर्हितम् ॥ 13 ॥
3.3.m:
And the antagonist is to be understood as one who conquers the world; / but the slaying of the antagonist is to be narrated, not of the other.
O great king, one should never depict the death of the hero; / one should depict it [only] for one who attains [heaven] in his own body.
Prose devoid of meter, contrary to grammar, / having an arrangement of words with harsh syllables, and accompanied by vulgar speech,
or in which the meaning of the sentences is hard to grasp, containing obscure expressions, / and what is repetitive—such poetic composition should not be made.
In wonder, or in indignation, in fear, sorrow, and haste, / and in joy, repetition should be employed; they do not consider that to be tautology.
In an envoy's speech, likewise in a dream, when an event has thus transpired through the course of affairs, / [or] in mentioning something again for further amplification—they consider that [too] not to be tautology.
[Speech] attended by doubt must not be uttered, nor [speech] lacking a proposition, / nor what is internally contradictory, nor that which is censured by the world.

3.3.m:
[A poem] should be endowed with the rasas named erotic, comic, pathetic, / furious, heroic, terrifying, odious, marvelous, and peaceful.
A poem endowed with artistic skill, supported by dharma and wealth, / should have a hero endowed with dharma, and should end only in his prosperity.
